articleTitle: A Novel High-Gain PAM4 Baud-Rate Phase Detector for ADC-Based CDR
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In this letter, we propose a novel high-gain four-level pulse amplitude modulation (PAM4) baud-rate phase detector (BRPD) for the ADC-based high-speed clock and data recovery (CDR) circuit. The PAM4 phase decisions are generated by three adjacent data and three adjacent error types. In addition, a linear model of the proposed PAM4 BRPD is developed for the first time to precisely calculate the gain, which is also critical for analyzing the key characteristics of the PAM4 BRPD-based CDR. Moreover, such a CDR is designed with 12nm CMOS technology and supplied with 0.8 voltage. The transistor simulation results show that the CDR can operate at 112 Gb/s, the RMS jitter of the recovered clock is 523 fs, and the CDR’s jitter tolerance meets the CEI-112G-LR-PAM4 mask.

articleTitle: Python Based Testbench for Coverage Driven Functional Verification
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: As digital design gets more complex, verification takes more efforts and it increasingly costs more than the design. The common verification practice of using the universal verification methodology (UVM)/system verilog (SV) has a higher entry barrier than using one of the most popular language Python. The paper uses the Python-based coroutine cosimulation testbench (cocotb) to verify a serial peripheral interface (SPI) and an advanced peripheral bus (APB) controller. The process of coverage driven verification from the test planning to the regression testing is discussed. The result confirms the correctness of the APB-SPI controller functions.

articleTitle: High Linearity Wide Band Passive Mixer for Ku-Band Applications in a 180nm CMOS Technology
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: A design of a passive mixer is presented. Linearity and bandwidth are the critical problems to mitigate in this work. Both up-conversion and down-conversion are supported. Fabricated in a 180nm CMOS technology, the mixer includes a LO active balun, a LO buffer and a RF passive balun. The LO buffer is designed to improve the sensitivity of LO signal. The mixer covers a wide RF frequency range of 6-18GHz. With a unique double-balanced passive mixer design, the resulted mixer achieves a 23.0dBm IIP3 at down-conversion, and a 23.4dBm IIP3 at up-conversion. The passive mixer attains −10.5dB conversion gain at down-conversion and −9.8dB conversion gain at up-conversion with LO driving at 0dBm. The DC power consumption of the proposed mixer is 500mW, due to the LO active balun and the LO buffer.

articleTitle: A Fully-Digital LDO with Adaptive Clock and Double-Edge-Triggered Shift Register for Quick Response
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper presents a digital low-dropout voltage regulator (DLDO) with fast transient response. When an overshoot or undershoot voltage occurs, a conventional DLDO operates a bi-directional shift register with a fast frequency to control the power transistor to turn on or off to restore the load voltage. If the response speed is increased, the clock frequency needs to be increased, which leads to an increase in power consumption. Therefore, the proposed DLDO structure with adaptive clocking and double-edge-triggered shift register it reduces the transient response time significantly while adaptively switching the high or low frequency clock to trade off power consumption and transient performance according to the load change, but it still has low ripple voltage. The proposed DLDO is implemented in a 180 nm CMOS process. The input and output voltage ranges are 0.6V to 1.0V and 0.55V to 0.95V. The overshoot and undershoot voltages at 0.6 V are 15S.37mV and 42.94mV, respectively, with a recovery time of 516. 4ns, quiescent current of 47.83$\mu$A, and current efficiency of 99.1% at a load current step from 1mA to 5mA.

articleTitle: High Precision Voltage Reference for ADC: Review and Design Methodology
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: High resolution analog-to-digital converters (ADCs) impose stringent accuracy requirements for the voltage reference, in terms of low temperature coefficient (TC), low noise, absolute accuracy and high driving capability. This paper reviews state-of-the-art circuit design techniques to implement a high precision ADC reference and the methodology to optimize the parameter metrics.

articleTitle: A Bandgap Reference Voltage Source Design for Wide Temperature Range
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: A bandgap reference voltage source circuit with a wide temperature range is designed. By introducing a substrate leakage current compensation circuit, the effect of substrate leakage effect on the bandgap reference output voltage is reduced, and a low temperature coefficient voltage output over a wide temperature range is achieved. The design is based on 0. 18um BCD process and simulated in Cadence environment. The results show that a stable voltage output with a temperature coefficient of 16.1ppm/° can be achieved over a wide temperature range of -40°C to +160°C with an output reference voltage of 1. 25V at 5V supply voltage.

articleTitle: High Performance Injection-Locked PLL Architectures: An Overview
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Low jitter phase locked loops (PLL) are widely used as clock generators and play a very critical role in various applications such as serial link or data converter systems. On the basis of conventional PLLs, researchers have invented sub-sampling, injection locking, and other techniques to improve the performance of PLL with constrained power and area. The injection-locked PLL (ILPLL) reduces the clock jitter by eliminating the accumulated jitter periodically. Because of the simple structure, the ILPLL has become the research focus in recent years. This paper reviews the development and application scenarios of ILPLLs.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Reference Current Source Based on Deep Submicron Technology
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: The reference current source has the advantages of low temperature coefficient and is not affected by the supply voltage. It is widely used in various analog circuits. Therefore, the study of reference current source is of great significance for the field of integrated circuits. In this paper, a reference current source with low temperature coefficient is designed and fabricated based on 0.18μm BCD process. The reference current source is based on the structure of the current summation mode, and the current with a positive temperature coefficient and the current with a negative temperature coefficient are summed and output, which improves its temperature coefficient. The test results show that when the operating voltage is 2.5 V, the quiescent current of the reference current source is 250 μ A. When the temperature is 25 °C, its output reference current is 10.84 μ A. The reference current source can generate a reference current with a temperature coefficient of $2.76\times 10^{\mathbf{-4}}~\mu{\mathrm {A}}$/°C in the temperature range of −20°C to 85°C.

articleTitle: Specific Emitter Identification Based on Feature Diagram Superposition
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Specific emitter identification (SEI) refers to individual emitter identification by analyzing hardware defect characteristics carried by received signals. Because distortion characteristics of components inside transmitter are complex and their differences are subtle, it is difficult to extract a single Radio frequency fingerprint (RFF) feature to improve recognition performance. Therefore, this paper proposes a novel SEI method based on feature diagram superposition. By constructing emitter distortion model and analyzing visual representation of different types of distortion, superimposed feature diagram can better reflect fingerprint features of different emitters compared to a single feature. Combining feature diagram superposition with neural network model, experimental simulation shows that the proposed method can enhance performance of individual emitter identification without increasing model complexity.

articleTitle: A 1-V 92.28-dB DR Sigma-Delta Modulator for Sensing Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: A Sigma-Delta modulator implemented in a 180 nm CMOS process is proposed with a supply voltage of 1 V. The modulator is targeted at sensing applications. The design of the modulator is optimized to achieve minimum power consumption and area. A larger signal input range at low voltage can be obtained by using rail-to-rail folded cascode amplifiers. 1/f noise in the low frequency band and modulator input offset are reduced using a chopper-stabilization technique. A dynamic range of 92.28 dB is achieved by the Sigma-Delta modulator over a 100 Hz signal bandwidth. The modulator core area is 0.1482 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and power consumption is 35 $\mu$W.

articleTitle: Non-idealities of N-Phase Passive Mixer and Its Canceling Methods
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: N-phase passive mixer first receivers have gained increasing attention for its inherent low power, wideband impedance match, out-of-band jammer tolerant, low noise Figure and bi-directional transparency for impedance transportation. However, the N-phase passive mixer still suffers from non-idealities such as clock overlap and parasitic introduced downward match frequency point offset (DMFO). In this work, these two non-idealities are analyzed and calculated, and an inductor choke technique for both clock overlap and DMFO cancellation is elaborated. The simulation results show that the proposed technique suppresses clock overlap as big as 3%. Moreover, with a relax requirement for clock overlap, the power of the N-phase clock generator was also optimized. The choke inductor also creates frequency pulling effect which can be simultaneously used to cancel the DMFO with no sacrifice of noise and power.

articleTitle: Study on 220GHz On-chip Transmission Structures with GaAs Process
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: 220GHz transmission structures for GaAs process are designed, which include suspended microstrip line, transition structures and low-pass filter. The paper makes a detailed theoretical analysis for design. Simulated results show that the cut-off frequency of 180$\mu$m-width microstrip line is 250GHz, the transmission loss in input and output transition structures are less than 1dB, low-pass filter’s transmission coefficient is less than −30dB for 200GHz~240GHz harmonic. Simulated results indicate all transmission structures have realized its function completely. It has great reference significance for terahertz monolithic integrated chip design.

articleTitle: A Two-Pin Trimming Circuit with Pre-trimming Function
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In actual production, due to the influence of the manufacturing process, there will be some deviations between the actual parameters and the design values of the chip, which will affect the performance of the chip. Based on the above problems, a two-pin trimming circuit design with pre-trimming function is proposed. This paper introduces the main characteristics, implementation process and coding protocol of the trimming circuit. Compared with the traditional trimming circuit, the pre-trimming function can determine the better trimming scheme. During the final trimming, multiple fuses can be melted at one time without repeated operation. The design of the ending fuse can avoid the problem of fuse melting by mistake that caused by signal fluctuation after trimming. The design of the chip is based on 30V 0.18$\mu{\mathrm {m}}$ BCD process, and the simulation results show that the design can meet the expected requirements.

articleTitle: A Low-Power Two-Step Time-to-Digital Conversion in 28 nm CMOS
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a two-step time-to-digital converter (TDC) using gated delay technique to reduce power consumption. To reduce power consumption gated delay technology turns the delay chain off when the arbiter is not sampling. Simulation results show that the TDC resolution can reach 7ps when fabricated in 28 nm CMOS process, and the power consumption is reduced by 60% compared to the conventional two-step TDC.

articleTitle: An Efficient Heterogeneous SoC with Reconfigurable CNN Accelerator for Edge Processing
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Convolutional neural networks (CNN) are widely used in intelligent image processing. Recently there is a trend that CNN has gain popular in edge device computing for near sensor processing which calls for both high processing ability and low power dissipation. In addition, there is a need to switch between different CNN models for better performance. To address on the above issues, this paper proposed an SoC chip architecture based on a sparsity-aware reconfigurable CNN accelerator. A zero skipping PE and hierarchy memory access was utilized for power saving. A reconfiguration method was proposed to change accelerator parameter without interrupting normal processing. The chip was fabricated in 28 nm CMOS process, the die size is 4.5mm $\times$ 4mm. The processing ability of the CNN accelerator reaches 0.8 TOPS at the frequency of 800 MHz while the power consumption of the whole chip is less than 4 W.

articleTitle: A Low Power Dynamic Comparator with Floating Inverter Amplifier for Column-Parallel ADC
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper presents a low power dynamic comparator for column-parallel Analog-to-Digital Converter (ADC) in CMOS image sensors (CIS). The pre-amplifier in the comparator is based on a floating inverter amplifier, which consists of an inverter-based input pair powered by a floating capacitor, achieves low power consumption. In addition, the preamplifier gain and dynamic power consumption of the comparator is insensitive to the input common-mode voltage. This circuit is implemented in TSMC 40nm CMOS process with a power supply of 0.9V. The simulation results show that the comparator achieves an accuracy of $500\mu \mathrm{V}$ and a power consumption of $2\mu \mathrm{W}$ with 40MHz comparison speed. Furthermore, the layout area is only $5\mu \mathrm{m}\times 35\mu \mathrm{m}$, reducing comparator area while achieving low power consumption.

articleTitle: A Programmable Delay-Controlling Technique for PVT Enhancement of Asynchronous SAR ADC
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: A 10-bit sub-1-V process-voltage-temperature (PVT) synthesis robust successive-approximation-register (SAR) analog-to-digital converter (ADC) is proposed for intelligent sensing applications. Due to the high degree of SAR ADC digitization, a sub-1-V power supply less than the nominal voltage is used to reduce the overall power consumption. However, compared with the nominal voltage for power supply, SAR ADC faces the problem of PVT instability at low voltage, the problem of asynchronous SAR ADC PVT instability is more severe. The traditional method of a fixed delay circuit can’t deal with all PVT deviations, which will lead to a decline in ADC yield. This paper presents a programmable delay-controlling technique for asynchronous SAR ADC. A 3-input decoder is used to adjust the current of the delay circuit to meet the delay required by ADC under various PVT combinations. Designed with a 0.11-$\mu \mathrm{m}$ CMOS process, the proposed SAR ADC occupies an area of 0.049 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.The design results indicate that when the sampling rate is 200 kS/s, under the five processes of TT, SS, FF, SF and FS, the power supply range of 0.9V~1V and the temperature range of −40°C~85°C, good dynamic characteristics are obtained. The power consumption is $2.24 \mu \mathrm{W}$ and the corresponding Figure of merit (FoM) is 16.46 fJ/Conversion-step at 0.95 V.

articleTitle: A Transfer Learning Approach for Electromagnetic Side-channel Attack and Evaluation
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Side channel analysis has posed a huge threat to cryptographic function security. And some mitigation techniques including masking and trace data desynchronization are used to prevent the adversary from attacking. In this article, we propose a transfer learning framework to attack this countermeasure and recover the secret key effectively and efficiently, which can not only reduce the trace number required for side channel attacks but also reduce the time to train deep learning models. We first deserve a well trained deep learning model by taking the simplest source trace synchronization dataset as the source domain. Then we migrate and adjust this well trained model to the target trace desynchronization dataset by pre-training, freezing, fine-tuning, etc. In addition, we implement four different deep learning models including AutoEncoder, CNN, MLP and ResNet into the transfer learning framework for fixed key scenario and variable key scenario to demonstrate the framework scalability and generality. Finally, we evaluate the transfer learning framework using the public ASCAD datasets. The experimental results show that our method can successfully recover the key with 75 traces on the ASCAD synchronous dataset, and the transfer learning framework can solve the situation that the signal is biased, it only needs 60 traces to recover the keys on the random offset 50 dataset, and only 75 to recover the keys on the random offset 100 dataset.

articleTitle: A K-Band High-Linearity and Low-Noise Down-Conversion Mixer in 65nm CMOS
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper presents a K-band down-conversion mixer in a 65nm CMOS process. To improve the conversion gain, linearity, bandwidth and noise Figure performance, instead of using the conventional Gilbert mixer, a transformer is introduced between the transconductance stage and the switching quad stage, realizing a radio-frequency (RF) common-source (CS) pre-amplifier and a current-mode passive mixer. With measurements, the down-conversion mixer achieves a conversion gain of 8 dB, a 3-dB bandwidth covering from 16 to 23 GHz, an input 1-dB compression point (IP1dB) of −8.3 dBm, an output 1-dB compression point (OP1dB) of −1.1 dBm and a noise Figure of 4.3 dB, while consuming 23-mW DC power consumption from a 1.2-V supply voltage.

articleTitle: 10GHz Low Current Mismatch Pseudo-Differential Charge Pump Phase-Locked Loop Circuit Design
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Design a 10GHz low current mismatch, low jitter fast locking charge pump phase-locked loop based on UMC 28nm HLP CMOS process. This design reduces the charge pump current mismatch by using a negative feedback loop method; the voltage-controlled oscillator uses a pseudo-differential structure to improve the frequency tuning range and proposes a low voltage high matching current mirror applied to the tail current switching control array to improve the robustness of the voltage controlled oscillator in a low voltage environment and reduce the phase noise of the voltage-controlled oscillator. The simulation results show that: the charge pump charge/discharge current mismatch is less than 2%; the voltage-controlled oscillator frequency tuning range is from 9.6 to 10. 4GHz, and the phase noise is -86.7dBc/Hz at the output frequency of 1MHz; the phase-locked loop lock time is 0. 75us, and the jitter is 2ps.

articleTitle: A Low-Power Cardiac Signal Processor for Atrial Fibrillation Detection with a Sensitivity of 93.02%
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: The paper presents a cardiac signal processor for power-efficient atrial fibrillation (AF) detection. The processor detects R-wave and AF based on Pan and Tompkins algorithm and Kolmogorov-Smirnov test (KS-test), respectively. Validated by MIT-BIH arrhythmia database, the AF detection sensitivity (SE) and specificity (SP) of 93.02% and 80.00% are achieved, respectively. The system operates at a clock frequency of 256 Hz significantly reducing the dynamic power, which makes it suitable for implantable cardiac monitor applications. The processor is implemented in a 180-nm CMOS process. It occupies an area of 1.45 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and consumes 11.758 $\mu$W at a 1.8-V supply.

articleTitle: Low Power Explicit-Pulsed Single-Phase-Clocking Dual-edge-triggering Pulsed Latch Using Transmission Gate
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: F1ip-flops/pulsed latches are one of the main contributors of power consumption in modern processors including GPU/AI processors. In this paper, a novel Low-Power Explicit-Pulsed Single-Phase-clock Dual-edge-triggering (LPP DET) Pulsed Latch using Transmission-gate is proposed. A novel XOR-based-circuit is used to detect input changes, create adaptive pulses, and eliminate redundant switching. In terms of power consumption, the LPP DET outperforms prior state-of-the-art DET, FS TSPC, by about 33.1% at 10% data switching activity and 1V in 45 nm technology using post-layout simulation.

articleTitle: Feasibility Analysis of New Energy Batteries Equipped on Conventional Submarines
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Through the analysis between the working principle of lithium-ion batteries and lead-acid batteries, and based on the research status of lithium-ion batteries at home and abroad, the safety performance of lithium-ion batteries for the submarine is analyzed. The problems faced by conventional submarines equipped with lithium-ion batteries in our country were sorted out. Basic requirements and feasibility analysis were made for applicability, safety and environmental protection, which provides a reference for solving the problem of lithium-ion batteries equipped on conventional submarines.

articleTitle: A Piezoelectric Energy Management Circuit Combining ReL-SSHI and MPPT for Impact-Type Piezoelectric Harvesters
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: To improve the output power of the impact-type piezoelectric energy harvesters (IPEHs), we present in this paper an energy management circuit that combines a bridge-rectifier-less synchronized switch harvesting on inductor (ReL-SSHI) rectifier and a maximum power point tracking (MPPT) method. The ReL-SSHI rectifier eliminates the effect of the inherent capacitance of IPEH through LC oscillation and enhances the output power without the use of diodes. The fractional open-circuit voltage (FOCV) method realizes the maximum energy extraction. The results demonstrated that the output power of the ReL-SSHI rectifier connected with the IPEH was 1.76 times that of the full-bridge rectifier (FBR). Moreover, the efficiency of the proposed energy management circuit reaches 93.2%.

Author Keywords: rectifier-less synchronized switch harvesting on inductor

articleTitle: An X-Band Microwave Switch Design
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Microwave switches are widely used to control the on-off or conversion of microwave signal transmission paths. In this paper, a SPDT (Single-Pole-Double-Throw) switch based on the X-band is designed, whose main function is to switch the input signal to two channels through the switch. The built-in limiter and low-noise amplifiers provide a certain channel gain for the system link, and realize the control of microwave signal outputs with different channels.

articleTitle: A 1.8-V 436-Microwatt 20-kHz Discrete-Time Dynamic Zoom ADC Based on a 2-Stage Floating Inverter Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper proposes a discrete-time (DT) dynamic zoom analog-to-digital converter (ADC). This ADC consists of a coarse 5-bit successive approximation register (SAR) ADC and a fine 1-bit third-order delta-sigma modulator (DSM), which obtains a high resolution efficiently. In this DSM, a highly energy-efficient, robust, and accurate loop filter is implemented by a 2-stage FIA. The ADC is designed and simulated in a 180-nm CMOS process with a sampling frequency (${\mathrm {f}}_{\mathrm{s}}$) of 6-MHz. The simulations show that the dynamic zoom ADC achieves 101.22-dB signal-to-noise-and-distortion ratio (SNDR) at 20-kHz bandwidth (BW), resulting in an SNDR-based Schreier Figure of merit (FoM) of 177.8-dB.

articleTitle: A Design of Full Ka-Band Power Amplifier in 65nm SOI CMOS
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: A full Ka-band millimeter-wave power amplifier (PA) with magnetic coupling resonator (MCR) matching network is designed in this paper which is based on 65nm SOI CMOS process. Impedance transformation is performed by MCR to achieve broadband impedance matching. The technology of neutralizing capacitor and source degeneration inductance is adopted to effectively improve the circuit performance. The simulation results of the amplifier show that at 28GHz, the saturated output power (Psat) is 20.1dBm, the output power 1dB compression point (P1dB) is 18.3dBm, and the peak power added efficiency (PAE) is 31.2%. The small-signal gain of 21.4dB and the 3dB bandwidth of is 21.5-41GHz, with a fractional bandwidth of 62%, which can cover the entire Ka-band.

articleTitle: A neural network PID controller with dynamic structure adjustment for DC-DC switching converters
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In this paper, a neural network PID controller with dynamic structure adjustment is proposed for DC-DC switching converters. To improve the efficiency of the controller and reduce its power consumption, the neural network for the proposed controller can change its structure adaptively in transient state according to the variation of voltage error, while it is disabled in steady state. Firstly, the whole voltage error range is divided into four parts to distinguish the location of voltage error. Then, the adaptive structure change mechanism is designed for neural network. Furthermore, a buck DC–DC switching converter using the proposed controller is designed and implemented on the field programmable gate array (FPGA) and printed circuit board (PCB). The experimental results demonstrated that it has similar transient performance in a DC-DC switching converter to that the conventional neural network PID controller, where neural network has the fixed structure. Meanwhile, the proposed controller has less power consumption and higher efficiency in transient state than a conventional neural network PID controller.

articleTitle: A Detection Method of Partial Discharge Signal Based on Wavelet
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: A wavelet is a rapidly decaying wavelike oscillation with zero mean. Wavelet transform is more suitable for analyzing various forms of non-smooth partial discharge signals than Fourier transform. Aiming at the common double exponential decay type partial discharge pulse, this paper studies the denoising effect of different wavelets, and compares the signal-to-noise ratio of the output signal, then selects the optimal one for the detection of partial discharge signal. The research results show that for the used wavelet, the partial discharge signal can be effectively detected while suppressing the noise interference.

articleTitle: A Double-Threshold Over-Temperature Protection Circuit for Smart Power ICs
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Smart power ICs often work in a high temperature environment, the junction temperature of the power MOSFET will be affected by the ambient temperature. Therefore, this work adds an ambient temperature sensor to detect the ambient temperature of the chip. When the ambient temperature is normal, the over-temperature threshold of the junction temperature sensor is adjusted to a high threshold, which can ensure the normal operation under high voltage and high current. When the ambient temperature is too high, the over-temperature shutdown threshold of the junction temperature sensor is adjusted to a low threshold, which prevent the thermal load on the chip caused by the untimely response of the junction temperature sensor. In addition, the temperature sensor designed in this paper uses the reverse current of the transistor to detect the temperature, which has the advantages of high sensitivity, simple circuit structure and low power consumption. The circuit is designed based on 60V0.35μm BCD process. The simulation results show that the over-temperature threshold of the ambient temperature sensor is $135^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$, and the hysteresis temperature is $5^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$. The junction temperature sensor has a high over-temperature threshold of $180^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$, a low over-temperature threshold of 1$50^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$, and all hysteresis temperature of 1$0^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$.

articleTitle: A 1-V 109.1-dB SNDR 185.2-dB FoMs DSM Based on An Output Swing Enhanced Gain-Boost Inverter
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper presents a single-loop 3rd-order single-bit delta-sigma modulator based on an output swing enhanced gain-boost inverter. Compared to the typical structures, the proposed output swing enhanced gain-boost inverter can improve DC gain and output swing simultaneously while only using typical threshold voltage devices, which can reduce cost and process complexity. The proposed inverter-based modulator is designed and simulated in a 180-nm CMOS process. Simulation results show that the modulator achieves a 109.1-dB SNDR in 2.5-kHz bandwidth while the power consumption is only 62-μW under a 1-V supply, leading to a 185.2-dB FoMs, which has a great application potential in internet of things (IoT) and wearable devices.

articleTitle: A Two-Step Single-Side Capacitor-Reversal High-Efficiency Switching Scheme for SAR ADCs
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper presents a highly efficiency, two-step capacitor-reversal switching scheme for successive approximation register (SAR) analog-to-digital converter (ADC). The proposed switching scheme combines a monotonic switching approach with a two-step architecture. The novel capacitor array structure has no switching energy consumption during the initial three comparison cycles. The energy reduction of the proposed switching scheme is 99.6% compared to the conventional SAR architecture with no reset energy. In addition, proposed switching scheme reduces the number of total capacitors in sample capacitors array by 73.4%, resulting in chip-area efficiency savings.

articleTitle: An 8-Bit 625MS/s SAR ADC for Sensor Application
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper presents an 8-bit 625MS/s SAR ADC for integrated sensor application. To enhance ADC conversion speed, the proposed SAR ADC generates 2-bit in one comparison cycle based on asynchronous mode, combining with two DAC arrays, SIG DAC and REF DAC. In addition, extra 1bit redundant is adopted to eliminate SIG DAC incomplete settling. By using a low kickback noise comparator with background offset calibration and minimizing the logic delay in the SAR decision loop, our ADC can achieve SNDR of 46.59 dB at 625MS/s rate under 1.2V supply voltage and maintain an ENOB higher than 7 bit up to Nyquist frequency.

articleTitle: A 12-Bit 100MSps Asynchronous SAR ADC with Improved Split Capacitive DAC
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper describes a 12-bit I00MS/s successive approximation register (SAR) analog-to-digital converter (ADC) and an improved split-capacitor digital-to-analog converter (DAC). The DAC adopts a two-stage structure bridged by unit capacitors, and the high fifth-order capacitors are equally divided. A control scheme combining splitting and monotony is adopted. This scheme can reduce power consumption and optimize the stability time of DAC without introducing common-mode reference voltage (Vcm). The ADC is fabricated using a 65nm CMOS process. The simulation results show that at 1. 2V supply voltage, the SNDR is 65. 4dB, the SFDR is 74. 7dB, and the power consumption is 4. SmW. The ADC core circuit size is 210um*180um, and the FoM is 31. 6fJ/Conv-step at Nyquist input frequency.

articleTitle: A Wideband Low Phase Noise Voltage Controlled Oscillator in 0.13μm CMOS
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: A wideband low phase noise (PN) voltage controlled oscillator (VCO) in 0.13$\mu$m CMOS technology is presented in this paper. In this work, the quality factors of inductor and capacitor are reduced, and the parasitic capacitor is increased, which leads to the deterioration of phase noise and the reduction of tuning range. A wide tuning range (TR) from 13.2 GHz to 21.5 GHz is obtained by varactor and 6-bit switch capacitor arrays, and the ${\mathrm {K}}_{\mathbf{VCO}}$ is less than 250 MHz/V. The low phase noise is realized by optimizing the LC tank quality factor and filtering the tail current source noise. The PN is −113 dBc/Hz@1MHz at the center frequency of 17.5 GHz. The current consumption is 25 mA from a 1.2 V supply, and the ${\mathrm {FOM}}_{\mathbf{T}}$ is −196.4 dBc/Hz.

articleTitle: Design of Broadband RF-PGA and DA in 0.13-μm CMOS
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: A radio frequency programmable-gain amplifier(RF-PGA) and a broadband driver amplifier utilizing differential cascode structure is proposed for gain adjustment in transmitter in this paper. Analysis of the Implementation of multi-bit gain step and optimization of layout have been presented based on $0.13-\mu$m CMOS process. The simulation results show that, after cascaded, the circuits achieve an output 1dB compression point $({\mathrm {OP}}_{\mathrm{1dB}})$ of 6.6-dBm at 1GHz, a ${\mathrm {S}}_{22}\lt -8$ dB, and 5.0-dB gain range with 0.25-dB step size over an opration frequency range of 0.05-7GHz.

articleTitle: A Low-Power High-Precision 12Bit SAR ADC
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper designs a 12-bit 6.67ksps successive approximation analog-to-digital converter (SAR ADC). The sampling and holding circuit uses MOS tube as sampling switch and adopts virtual switch and lower plate sampling to improve sampling accuracy. The comparator adopts a dynamic comparator structure composed of two-stage pre-amplification and latch, which reduces the power consumption of the comparator and improves the speed of the comparator. The DAC module adopts a segmented resistance tree structure, which effectively reduces the design difficulty and improves the accuracy of the DAC module. The design and simulation are based on 0.35$\mu$m BCD process. Under 6.67ksps, the conversation range of ADC is 0-2.56V, the power consumption is 40.59$\mu$A, the DNL is −0.8/+0.4LSB, the SNR is 68.146dB, and the SFDR is 85.781dB, ENOB is 11.027bit.

articleTitle: Design of a High Gain Dual Frequency Butterfly Dipole Antenna
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In this paper, a high-gain dual-frequency butterfly dipole antenna is designed. The antenna adopts the shape of a butterfly dipole, which plays a role in expanding the bandwidth of the antenna. Two pairs of butterfly patches with different sizes realize the dual-band characteristics of the antenna, and the form of binary array is used to improve the gain of the antenna., the feeding method adopts 50 ohm coaxial feeding. The designed antenna is processed into a fabricated prototype and tested. The results show that the antenna can work well in two frequency bands of 2.4–2.5GHz and 5.15–5.85GHz. When the antenna works at lower frequency, the return loss is less than −10dB, and the maximum gain can reach 9dBi; when it works at higher frequency, the return loss of the antenna is less than 10dB, and the maximum gain can reach 7dBi. The antenna has the advantages of low cost, small size, simple structure, easy integration with microwave circuits, etc., and can be applied to wireless communication fields such as WLAN, RFID, WiMax, and LTE.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study of High Speed Optical Receiver Implementation in CMOS, SiGe, SOI, and FinFET
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: A comparison between high speed optical receivers implanted using different technologies such as CMOS, SiGe, SOI, and FinFET is presented. We discuss important design trade-offs in these technologies in terms of speed, sensitivity and power dissipation. We conclude that CMOS technology outperforms SiGe, SOI, and FinFET technology in terms of power consumption while matching speed and sensitivity at data rate below 40Gbps. At higher rate, however, SiGe technology is preferred because of the high speed and high gain, but at the cost of higher power dissipation. The selection of technology for optical receiver implementation should take into account the speed, sensitivity, power consumption, and wafer cost of the required final product.

articleTitle: A High Precision Voltage Detection Circuit for Multiple Lithium Batteries
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In order to meet the demand of high-precision voltage sampling of multiple lithium batteries, a high-precision voltage detection circuit aiming at the safety problems during battery use is proposed in this paper. The reference voltage generates a high-precision threshold voltage through the resistor divider network, and the sampling voltage is improved by using the principle of capacitance divider. The circuit uses time-division multiplexing to achieve voltage detection function, a comparator detects multiple threshold voltages, so the circuit structure is concise. The structure can be used for multi-section series battery packs, significantly reducing the chip area. According to the comparison results, the working state of the battery is judged, and corresponding protective measures are taken to achieve the purpose of protecting the lithium battery. The circuit is implement using a 30V 0.18$\mu$ m BCD (Bipolar-CMOS-DMOS) technology. Simulation results show that the overcharge voltage detection accuracy is 0.78mV and the over-discharge voltage detection accuracy is 0.63mV.

articleTitle: Voltage Detection Circuit with Delay for Power Management Circuits
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Power management circuits that have stable output voltage can provide reliable power supply for other circuits and chips. However, in some cases, the magnitude of the power supply may fall below a threshold voltage, which has a negative effect on its load circuit. This paper presents a voltage detection circuit with delay for monitoring the output voltage of power management circuits, which can detect an undervoltage condition on the output voltage and generate a power-on reset (POR) signal with a delay time that can be set. The delay time generator only works within the setting delay time, thus, the quiescent current consumption can be reduced and then the efficiency of the power management will be improved. The voltage detection circuit with delay is implemented in a $0.18 \mu \mathrm{m}$ CMOS process with an active area of 0.039 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, operating in the voltage ranging from 1.8 V to 3.3 V. The proposed circuit consumes 3.3 $\mu \mathrm{A}$ of quiescent current during the setting time and 1.55 $\mu \mathrm{A}$ of quiescent current when the oscillator and the timer do not work. The threshold voltage is 95% of the output voltage and the delay time is set to 20 ms.

articleTitle: A Low-Noise, High-Linearity Amplifier for Wireless Base-Stations
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In this paper, a 0.1–1.5 GHz high-linearity low noise amplifier (LNA) is designed based on a 0.5 $\mu$m GaAs pHEMT process, which employs one stage 2-stacked-FETs to obtain a broadband gain performance and wideband impedance matching. Biasing with a 5 V drain voltage and 101 mA quiescent current, this LNA shows measurement results of about 0.1-watt power performance in the frequency range of 0.1–1.5 GHz with a output third-order intercept point (OIP3) of above 39 dBm. The measured S-parameters show a gain (S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</inf>) of 13 to 25 dB, a maximum input return loss (S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>) of −19 dB, a maximum output return loss (S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">22</inf>) of −12 dB. The chip occupies a small chip size of $0.7 \times 0.65$ mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. Using a loadpull system, this LNA can maintain high OIP3 of above 35 dBm against a wide load impedance range.

articleTitle: Analysis and Compensation of Horizontal Attitude Error of Low-Cost Manipulator Front End
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper presents a control method for the large horizontal attitude error of the front end of the low-cost six degree of freedom light manipulator. According to the angle position model of the manipulator, the inverse motion equation is established and the joint angles are obtained by inverse solution; Test the linear error of the 3, 4 and 5 joint actuator of the manipulator in the process of rotation and fit the compensation straight line; By calculating the center of gravity position of the control object divided by 3, 4 and 5 joints under no-load condition and simulating the joint error in MATLAB, a hierarchical compensation method for nonlinear error is proposed; By analyzing the physical characteristics of the manipulator, the dead zone range is obtained under the condition that the front-end attitude remains horizontal. Combined with the compensated target position, whether the end of the manipulator will enter the dead zone is judged. Through the manipulator experiment, the error compensation method successfully reduces the horizontal error of the front end of the manipulator from ± 14mm to ± 4mm.

articleTitle: An Injection-Locked Frequency Multiplier with Wide Locking-Range in 28-nm CMOS
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper presents a high conversion gain broadband millimeter wave injection-locked frequency multiplier (ILFM) in 28-nm CMOS technology. In order to obtain a wider locking range, the on-chip transformers is used to inject harmonic signal to optimize the phase response of the coupled resonator. In order to improve the output signal power, the improved push-push structure are used to enhance the output power. The simulation results show that the power supply voltage of the ILFM is 0.9V, a frequency locking range of 38 - 52GHz, a core power consumption of 9mW, a core area of 0.063mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, and a signal output power greater than 0dBm.

articleTitle: Study on Antireflection Film Based on Nano Pore
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Optical anti-reflection film is an important branch of thin film optics, and its application spreads throughout all fields of optics. Generally, the materials for preparing optical anti-reflection films are magnesium fluoride, calcium fluoride and some fluorinated polymer polymers with good thermal stability so that the equivalent refractive index of the substrate and the film is reduced, and then the substrate refractive index matches the air refractive index to achieve the purpose of increasing anti-reflection. The characteristics of these materials are that they all have a relatively low refractive index. Among these materials, its application is most common due to the low refractive index of magnesium fluoride (MgF2, refractive index 1.38). However, if a magnesium fluoride film is coated with glass as a substrate, it still has a reflection loss of about 1.5%. Polymer nanoporous films can achieve a relatively low refractive index, thereby achieving the refractive index requirements of high transmittance anti-reflection films on the refractive index of materials; The spin coating film preparation process adopted is simple and the preparation cost is low; In terms of optical properties, the anti-reflection effect of polymer nanoporous films is also far superior to that of traditional anti-reflection films. In addition, its most prominent advantage is that the refractive index specified nanoporous polymer film can be obtained through the control of porosity, which will make the nanoporous polymer film widely used in optical films and optoelectronic devices and other fields. In this paper, a low refractive index thin film material with adjustable refractive index is prepared by using nanophase separation technology of polymer materials to meet the needs of various substrate pairs of anti-reflection films. This paper introduces the principle of increasing anti-reflection, the preparation of thin films and their optical performance tests.

articleTitle: A Novel FinFET Device with a Four-Period Vertically Stacked SiGe/Si Fin
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In this work, a novel four-period vertically stacked SiGe/Si FinFET is demonstrated to further boost the electrical performance of the FinFET device. The stacked SiGe/Si fin structure was fabricated successfully by developing the stacked SiGe/Si epitaxial growth and etching processes. Compared with the conventional SiGe channel FinFET, the driven current ION and ION/IOFF ratio of this novel FinFET device increased by 1.6 and ~10 times, respectively. Meanwhile, its subthreshold slope (SS) was improved from 149mV/dec to 90 mV/dec. The improvement of electrical performance can be attributed to the high quality SiGe layer, increased effective channel width, and excellent surface interface properties throughout the whole fabrication process. More importantly, after employing an optimized O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> passivation technique, its SS and ION/IOFF ratio can be further improved to 75mV/dec and $5\times{10}^{6}$, respectively. The above results strongly suggest that this novel stacked SiGe/Si channel FinFET device is a promising candidate for future technology nodes.

articleTitle: A Broadband ADPLL Design with Automatic Mode Change
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This article introduces the all-digital phase-locked loop (ADPLL) designed by Verilog. Pango Design Suite is used to provide the basic modules of ADPLL. Aiming at the narrow frequency band and slow speed of traditional ADPLL, the following improvements are made. The frequency monitoring module is added to broaden the phase-locked range. The automatic mode change control module is added to accelerate the locking speed. Under the system clock of 100MHz, the frequency range that can be locked is about 762.96Hz-250KHz. The frequency resolution can be as low as 0.01Hz and as high as 1.2KHz.

articleTitle: Low Noise Front-end Readout ASIC for 3D Position-Sensitive Pixelated CdZnTe detector
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This work presents a low-noise and low-power front-end readout ASIC for 3D position-sensitive Cadmium-Zinc-Telluride (CZT) detectors. The application specific integrated circuit (ASIC) is capable of reading out energy and timing signals from 64 anode pixels and one cathode electrode of pixelated CZT detector simultaneously. Each anode channel provides low-noise charge amplification, high-order shaping, baseline holding, along with peak and timing detection. The input charge ranges from 0.7 fC to 35 fC, corresponding to the particle energy of 20 keV to 1 MeV. The simulation results show that the equivalent noise charge (ENC) of the anode channel is better than 130 $e^{-}$ at a 3 pF input capacitance, and ENC of the cathode channel is better than 300 $e^{-}$ at a 6 pF input capacitance. The time resolution of the anode channel is better than 11 ns at an input charge of 2 fC, and cathode channel is better than 16.5 ns. The power consumption of one channel is less than 2.5 mW with event rate up to 100 ksps.

articleTitle: An Operational Amplifier with High EMI-Immunity in Battery Management System for New Energy Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: A CMOS fully differential push-pull (FDPP) operational amplifier (Op Amp) is proposed with high gain and electromagnetic interference (EMI) immunity. The operating principle of this work is described and the structure is provided. The proposed Op Amp focuses on the application of new energy vehicles and it helps improve circuit robustness and reliability. The circuit is designed in $0.35\mu \mathrm{m}60\mathrm{V}$ Bipolar-CMOS-DMOS (BCD) Technology with a supply voltage of 5V to achieve 86dB gain, with a 10° phase margin, unity gain frequency (UGF) of 12MHz, static power consumption of 3mW, and full swing input. Measurements of EMI-induced input offset confirm the circuit simulation. The input offset voltage is only 0. 2mV with 2. 4GHz 1Vpp EMI. After simulation verification, this Op Amp can be used for BMS chips of new energy vehicles.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Reconfigurable RS Processor
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: As a representative error correction code, Reed-Solomon code is widely used in the related fields of information transmission and storage for its excellent performance. Application Specific Integrated Circuit (ASIC) is a mainstream hardware implementation solution. Although it has a high energy efficiency ratio, it has poor flexibility and cannot be applied to other communication environments. It needs to be redesigned and tape-out according to the application requirements, and the cost is enormous. Given the above problems, this paper proposes a coarse-grained reconfigurable processor suitable for RS encoding and decoding technology, which can meet the requirements of Forward Error Correction (FEC) technology in different communication scenarios. The design can conFigure RS codec circuits with different codes, different code lengths and different degrees of parallelism according to the instructions, and can support dynamic configuration of the processor under the condition that the total code length is constant and the signal code length is adjustable. There are broad application prospects in terms of flexibility.

articleTitle: A Low BER DB-PAM4 Adaptive Equalizer For Large Channel Loss In Wireline Receiver
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In order to solve the problem of large channel loss and high bit error rate in high-speed signal transmission of wireline receiver, an adaptive equalizer suitable for 112 Gb/s DBPAM4 is designed in this paper. In order to avoid the problem that the equalization capability of the adaptive equalizer is limited after the PAM4 signal undergoes large channel loss, this paper designs the DB-PAM4 encoding based on the dou-binary encoding technology of NRZ, which improves the equalization capability of the receiver, The DB-PAM4 signal replaces the PAM4 signal, reducing the signal transmission bandwidth. In order to solve the problems of complex adjustment and low equalization accuracy in traditional adaptive equalization, a twostep equalization method is adopted for adjustmen. First, use the conversion process of NRZ signal to Doubinary signal to generate a data path with duobinary characteristics, then send the prepam4 signal to adjust the tap coefficient of the DSP. This paper uses Cadence’s AMS simulation platform to verify the receive equalizer of DB-PAM4. Simulation results show: When 112Gb/s pre-PAM4 signal passes through 35dB@28GHz channel, receiver(RX) utilizes adaptive equalizer to generate 112Gb/s DBPAM4 signal, and the receiver bit error rate (BER) is less than 3e-9.

articleTitle: A 2.3-2.7 GHz Power Amplifier with Piecewise Adaptive Bias and Reactance Compensated Interstage Matching Network in 130nm SOI LDMOS Process
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper presents a 2.3-2.7GHz SOI LDMOS power amplifier for LTE applications. By using the adaptive bias (ADB) technique, the linear output power range is expanded. The piece-wise response ADB circuit is introduced to avoid gain expansion generated by ADB when PA has soft compression. At the same time, a reactance compensated inter-stage matching technique is designed for better performance consistency at different frequencies. The output 1-dB compressed power and saturated output power are 31.29dBm and 33.4dBm. The peak power added efficiency is 53.33%.

articleTitle: A 20Gbps CTLE with Active Inductor
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper presents a continuous-time linear equalizer (CTLE) with active inductor loads in parallel with low frequency branches. The proposed equalizer is realized with active inductor technology and the combination of low and mid frequency circuits separates the zeros of the output function in a 5:1 ratio, significantly enhancing the high frequency gain. The data is equalized by a cascade of two equalizers with different circuit structures to compensate for the damaged signal in turn. Implemented in CMOS 2S nm technology, for the data rate of 20 Gbps, the equalizer achieves a 0. 85UI eye width, and 10.37 dB channel loss at the Nyquist frequency.

articleTitle: A Chopper Amplifier with Low Offset and Low Noise for Temperature Controllers
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: For high precision integrated temperature controllers, the low frequency noise and offset voltage will affect the accuracy. The chopper stabilization technology can eliminate the offset and 1/f noise through modulation, transfer and filtering signal processing technology. In general, these technologies require a sacrifice of power consumption and area. This work is based on BCD 250nm process, and this paper introduce a chopper amplifier with low offset and low noise, the simulation results show that it has 9. 6uA, 0.23mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> consumption, 13.7 nV$\sqrt{}$Hz input noise density, and < 2.5uv offset voltage.

articleTitle: A Wideband Low-Noise Amplifier in 0.13-µm CMOS
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper designs a wideband low-noise amplifier (LNA) covering wideband of 7-18 GHz. This wideband LNA design adopts the shunt-series peaking technique to improve the high frequency gain response, and three-stage amplifier further extends the bandwidth (BW). The unique properties of ladder filter are used to match an inductively degenerated transistor to a 50 $\Omega$source over a wide band. Based on the 0.13-$\mu$m CMOS process, the simulation results show that the wideband LNA achieves a gain flatness of 22 ± 0.5 dB in the range of 7-18 GHz, the return loss (S$_{\mathbf{11}}$) is less than −9.6 dB, the whole circuit noise Figure (NF) is 2.29-2.7 dB.

articleTitle: Exploration of Using Direct Programming Interface to Improve the Reusability of Verification IP
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Discuss UVM reusability, build APB_I2C IP verification environment through direct programming interface, successfully realize multi-language collaborative verification, and verify the feasibility of vertical reuse of C test cases from module level to subsystem level through the virtual processor scheme. Using the coverage-driven strategy, the verification progress is quantified, and the verification goal of 100% coverage is finally achieved, which improves the completeness and accuracy of verification. Finally, the cross-type debugging library is used to quickly locate and verify the error position in the simulation, which greatly shortens the verification cycle of the SoC.

articleTitle: A 26 GHz Power Amplifier with 26.4 dB Power Gain and 22.1 dBm Output Power in 65 nm CMOS
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In this paper, a 26 GHz two-stage differential CMOS power amplifier (PA) is proposed for 5G communication with 65-nm CMOS process. A differential capacitive-neutralized common source gain cell is used to maintain the stability as well as to boost the gain and output power performance. Meanwhile, to achieve good overall performance, the output and inter-stage impedances of the PA are optimized by balancing the amplifier power gain, power added efficiency (PAE) and output power. A low loss four-way transformer-based power combining network is adopted in this PA to achieve high gain and output power performance. With measurements, the PA achieves a peak gain of 26.4 dB at 26 GHz with a bandwidth from 24.7 to 28.5 GHz. At 1dB compression and saturated points, the PA delivers an output power and PAE of 18.8/22.1 dBm and 15.97/33.26%, respectively. The core chip area without pads is 0.805 mm$^{\mathbf{2}}$.

articleTitle: Design of a P-JFET Compatible with CMOS Technology
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Starting from the process conditions of P-channel JFET, this paper analyzes the influence of main process parameters on key parameters such as device pinch-off voltage, breakdown voltage, and on-resistance. Based on the working requirements of the blocking surge protector, it is necessary to design a P-type conductive channel JFET device with a pinch-off voltage of 9.5V and a breakdown voltage of 20V. The structure and electrical performance of the device are simulated by TCAD simulation software, and the influence of each parameter is verified by actual tape-out. The actual tape-out data show that when the injection dose of PW is 2E12cm-2, the epitaxial thickness is 5um, and the buried layer is a single antimony injection, the P-type conductive channel JFET device can meet the design requirements, which has certain guiding significance for the production of related junction FET devices.

articleTitle: A Low Power PLL Circuit with Area-Saving Loop Filter Applied in MEMS
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper presents a Phase-Locked Loop (PLL)circuit with low power consumption and an area-saving on-chip loop filter. Designed for a Gyro Micro Electro Mechanical System (MEMS), the circuit is capable of providing different clock signals with different frequencies and phases for the Gyro system. Implemented with a TSMC 0.18-$\mu$ m CMOS process, the proposed PLL has a working range of llkHz-5.63MHz with 1.5mW power consumption, It occupies a core chip area of 0.1mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: A 0.8-1.8 GHz Low Noise Amplifier for 5G Application
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In this paper, a 0.8-1.8 GHz monolithic low noise amplifier (LNA) is designed and fabricated based on the 0.5 $\mu$m GaAs pHEMT process. By utilizing two cascode amplifiers as gain cells, high gain bandwidth product and high linearity are obtained in this LNA. To achieve the wideband response and low chip size, a self-biasing circuit combing the RC negative feedback technique is employed in this LNA. Basing with 67 mA at 5 V, measured results of this LNA show a gain (S21) of 15 ± 0.3dB, a input/output return loss (S11 and S22) of -15 dB and -20 dB, a 1dB output compression point (P1dB) of about 19 dBm, a input third-order intercept point (IIP3) of above 10.5 dBm within the frequency range of 0. 8-1.8GHz. The LNA occupies a small chip size of 0.7× 0.65mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. Thus, the application requirement in 5G communication system can be met by this LNA.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Quenching and Active Reset Circuit for High-Speed SPAD Detectors
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper presents a hybrid quenching and active reset circuit for high-speed single-photon avalanche diode (SPAD) detectors based on a standard 180 nm CMOS process. A hybrid quenching scheme combining cascaded passive quenching and variable-load quenching is employed to both reduce the response time of the front-end circuit from sensing the avalanche current to quenching it, and extend the quenching and recharging voltage range limited by the maximum allowable operation voltage of standard transistors. Simulation is performed based on a modified SPAD model built with Verilog-A language and ideal switches. Simulation results indicate that the sensing and quenching time is about 300 ps. Meanwhile, the quenching and reset voltage range provided by the front-end circuit is significantly improved from 1.8 V to 3 V. In addition, the hybrid quenching and active reset circuit is tunable, achieving a minimum dead time of about 2 ns.

articleTitle: An Adaptive Equalizer for 56 Gb/s Duo-Binary SerDes
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Aiming at the problem that the traditional non-return-to-zero code in the high-performance network seriously influences the channel attenuation and high bit error rate in the backplane high-speed communication, this paper proposes an adaptive equalizer based on 56Gb/s Duo-Binary as an alternative to PAM4. The Duo-Binary signal is generated by utilizing the channel loss to improve the channel transmission bandwidth, which reduces the complexity of subsequent equalization processing. To solve the problems of complex traditional blind adaptive algorithm and low equalization intensity, the transmitter adopts forward feedback equalization, and the receiver adopts two-stage CTLE and 2-tap half-rate DFE for adaptive equalization. Adaptive equalization uses the least mean square algorithm to adjust the CTLE control signal and DFE tap coefficients. The overall performance of the system is verified by AMS simulation in Cadence IC. Under the 28nm TSMC process, the 56Gb/s Duo-Binary signal can compensate for the channel loss of more than 35dB, and the bit error rate is less than 4e-12 using PRBS7.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Hard-Decision LDPC Decoder
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Hard-decision LDPC decoders are widely used in communication and storage systems due to their simple circuits. However, existing hard decision LDPC decoding circuits lead to slow decoding convergence due to flipping according to the maximum energy value, reducing decoding performance. This paper proposes the Dual-Energy Probabilistic Gradient Descent Bit-Flipping (DPGDBF) hard-decision algorithm. If the energy value of the variable node reaches the threshold, all nodes with the threshold energy will be flipped, and the node with the sub-maximum threshold energy will be flipped with a certain probability. otherwise, only all variable nodes with the maximum energy value are flipped. The simulation results show that, in a limited iterative range, compared with Tabu-list Random-Penalty Gradient Descent Bit-Flipping (TRGDBF), for (2048, 1024) codes, the average number of decoding iterations of the algorithm is reduced by 12%, and the decoding performance is improved to a certain extent; for (9216,7680) codes, the average number of decoding iterations of the DPGDBF algorithm is reduced by 18%, and the decoding performance is improved by 4 times. In addition, this paper proposes a hardware implementation of the DPGDBF algorithm for (2048, 1024) codes, with a maximum clock frequency of 305.53MHz and a through-put of 19.52Gbps.

articleTitle: A Novel All-Digital on-Chip Aging Sensor Robust to Process Variations
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: With the development of semiconductor technology, the reliability of integrated circuit (IC) is challenged by multiple aging mechanisms, which could increase the delay of ICs and cause timing violations. Hence, it is necessary to monitor the aging degree of the IC in real time. In this paper, we present a novel on-chip aging sensor based on path delay measurement, which can perform accurate measurement in two clock cycles. The proposed sensor is all-digital with low area overhead. Experiment result shows that the random measurement error is less than 2.92ps during 2 years aging. In addition, the sensor is robust to process variations.

articleTitle: High-Performance Inkjet Printed OLEDs Realized by Improved Film Morphology
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Inkjet printing technology with the characteristic of patterned deposition shows great potentials in manufacturing cost-effective and large-area organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs). However, the poor film morphology caused by “Coffee-Ring” effect in inkjet printed OLEDs (IJP OLEDs) is detrimental to develop efficient and stable device. In this work, we demonstrate that outward radial capillary flow can be retarded by increased ink viscosity, thus the “Coffee-Ring” effect has been effectively relieved. With the improved film morphology, current efficiencies (CEs) of IJP OLED were increased by 18%, more importantly, a twofold enhancement in device lifetime was also realized.

articleTitle: A 0.5V,16.67nW,0.107%/V ALL-CMOS Subthreshold Voltage Reference with PSRR Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: An improved high power supply reject ratio (PSRR), all-CMOS sub-threshold voltage reference is proposed in this paper. A novel PSRR-up structure composed of a simple transconductance amplifier and a PMOS operating in linear region is put forward in our reference. Due to PMOS-bulk-driven and sub-threshold technology, our reference can produce a stable voltage at 0.5V power supply voltage. In addition, a novel double start-up circuit is presented to reduce the start time and a process-trim module is also used to reduce the impact of different corners. The simulation results show that the linear sensitivity is 0.107%/V in the range of 0.5V to 1.8V power supply voltage by designed in a standard $0.18 \mu \mathrm{m}$ CMOS process. The temperature coefficient (TC) is 32.49 ppm/°C across a range of $- 40^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ to $85^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$. Due to proposed PSRR-improved structure, a PSRR over 63.92dB can be obtained at 100Hz with only 16.67nW power consumption.

articleTitle: Event-Driven While-Loop Circuits
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Asynchronous circuits are predicted to play a very important role in future chip designs. However, asynchronous circuit design techniques are not yet well-established. This is due to the lack of powerful design toolkits and convenient building blocks. In this paper, an asynchronous building block is proposed and implemented to realize the loop structure which is mostly used in algorithms. The block works in an event-driven methodology, and is verified by an event-driven data stability detection circuit.

articleTitle: A Ka Band Based-on GaAs Asymmeteric Single-Pole Double-Throw Switch
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper introduces a single-pole, double-throw switch MMIC based on GaAs Pseudomorphic High Electron Transistor (PHEMT) technology for 5G mmWave front-end applications. It is based on an asymmetric structure which maintains high power handling capability, low insertion loss and compact structure in the 35-40GHz operating frequency band. The simulated results of the proposed switch achieves an insertion loss of 0.9/2.0 dB in Tx/Rx operation mode and an isolation of 27dB in Tx mode. When operating in Tx mode, the simulated result of an input 1dB compression point (IP1dB) is 36dBm at 38GHz. The chip area is 0.94mm $\times1.6$ mm.

articleTitle: Digital Amplitude Control and Time-Division Multiplexing Detection ASIC for Horizontal DualAxis Silicon Micro-gyroscope
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper describes a digital amplitude control and time-division multiplexing detection ASIC for horizontal dual-axis silicon micro-gyroscope. The digital drive amplitude control circuit effectively reduces the 1/f noise and improves the temperature stability of the system. At the same time, it realizes the fast and stable amplitude startup of the closed-loop drive. The time-division multiplexing detection circuit effectively reduces the power consumption and area of the dual-axis gyro-detection circuit, and improves the integration level of the system, and prevents the occurrence of signal crosstalk between two axes. Firstly, we establish an analysis model of closed-loop gyroscope drive amplitude control system, and digital PI controller is employed to realize low-noise amplitude control and fast startup. The simulation results show that the closed-loop drive amplitude setting time is 0.2s. Secondly, in the detection channel, the ADC and digital demodulation and preprocessing circuit in the detection circuit are multiplexed. The 2kHz select signal is used to complete the time-sharing output of the two outputs. The experimental results show that the angle random walk of the dual-axis silicon micro-gyroscope is $0.03^{\circ}/ h^{1/2}$.

articleTitle: A High-Accuracy Over-Temperature Protection Circuit with Adjustable Threshold for DC-DC
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In order to protect DC-DC chip from over-temperature damage, a high-accuracy over-temperature protection circuit is proposed in this paper. The temperature sensor was realized by cascaded transistors to obtain higher detection accuracy. The hysteresis temperature could be set by the voltage divider circuit, which was proportional to the value of the connected resistance. So the implementation of the circuit was simplified. The circuit is fabricated on a 5V180 nm BCD technology. The simulation results show that when the supply voltage is 5V, the over-temperature threshold is about 160°C and the temperature hysteresis is about 30°C. With the supply voltage varying between 2. 5V and 5. 5V, the drift of the over temperature threshold and that of the hysteresis temperature are 1. 03°C and 1. 35°C, respectively.

articleTitle: Design of Software-Hardware Collaborative Graph Computing Accelerator Based on RISC-V
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: The irregularities in the execution process of graph computing applications lead to the existing common architecture facing huge challenges in computing, accessing and other aspects. Dedicated accelerators can improve computing performance, but it is difficult to effectively cope with characteristics such as poor locality of graph data. Combining the respective advantages of a common architecture and a dedicated accelerator can effectively alleviate the challenges of graph computing today. In this paper, based on RISC-V oriented connected component and minimum spanning tree algorithm, a software and hardware cooperative graph computing accelerator and a special co-processor instruction are designed, and an instruction compilation environment and acceleration function library are established. Based on the MCU 200T platform, this paper uses p2pGnutella05, wikiVote, Facebook_combined and DaysALL data sets to prototype the accelerator. The results show that the accelerator designed in this paper reduces the resources by 75.6% compared with the mainstream accelerator HitGraph, and reduces the resources by 97.5% compared with the accelerator designed with high parallelization. The power consumption of the connected component algorithm accelerator decreased by 92.3%, the throughput increased by $1.65 \times$, and the power efficiency increased by $16.27 \times$; the power consumption of the minimum spanning tree algorithm accelerator decreased by 82.1%, the throughput increased by $1.44 \times$, and the power efficiency increased by $8.16 \times$.

articleTitle: An Order-Reduced Memory Polynomial Behavioral Model for RF Power Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper presents a behavioral model of order-reduced memory polynomial (ORMP) for digital predistortion (DPD) in RF power amplifiers. After iterative training with Greedy-Search method and Model-Growth technique, the proposed ORMP model with additional crossing terms achieves better predistortion performance and lower complexity compared with other DPD techniques. The effectiveness of the proposed model is verified by the measurement results of a switched capacitor power amplifier (SCPA). For LTE 10MHz64 QAM PAPR S.4dB signal, the EVM is improved by 6. 144dB and the ACPR is improved by 6. 189dB. For LTE 20MHz64 QAM PAPR 8. 4dB signal, the EVM and ACPR are improved by 4. 723dB and 2. 542dB respectively.

articleTitle: Memory Compiler for RRAM In-Memory Computation
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: The ”storage wall” and ”power consumption wall” brought by von Neumann architecture begin to restrict the development of SOC. In order to solve the problem caused by the traditional architecture, the concept of in-memory computing is proposed. As a new type of memory, RRAM is very suitable for designing memory computing architecture. This paper presents an RRAM memory compiler for in-memory computation. Compared with the traditional memory compiler, the RRAM in-memory computing compiler has high flexibility and is reconfigurable by organizing various existing computing modules and peripheral circuits. By constantly enriching the module library, more use scenarios are met and rapid development is realized.

articleTitle: A 13-Bit 150-Ms/s Hybrid SARADC Based on VTC on the Fine Stage
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: A 13bit150Ms/s hybrid ADC is proposed in this paper. The first stage is designed to be a 10-bit SARADC to coarsely quantize the input level, and then the voltage residual is transferred to the time domain through a current adjustable VTC, and then TDC is used for the remaining 3bits quantify. In order to reduce the mismatch caused by the capacitor array, the DAC is divided into a 7-b BDAC controlled by the high-order thermometer code and a 3-b SDAC controlled by the low-order binary code, helping to improve the capacitor turnover speed and utilization rate, mismatch and so on, which means that the subsequent quantization can be completed without re-sampling the residual with another set of capacitors. The characteristic of good linearity helps to improve the quantization accuracy. In the T40 CMOS process, simulations show that the ADC achieves 68. 3dB SFDR and 9. 2mW power consumption.

articleTitle: Design of Fast Start-up CMOS RC Oscillator Based on Low Temperature Coefficient Current Mode Bandgap Reference
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper presents a fully integrated 2MHz RC oscillator which is less affected by the fluctuations of power supply voltage and ambient temperature. This design consists of a current mode bandgap reference circuit and an RC oscillation circuit. Furthermore, a digital trimming circuit is used to adjust the frequency back to the ideal one, in order to obtain better accuracy.
