The proposed current mode bandgap reference has a very low temperature coefficient, which is only 1.66ppm/°C. This RC oscillator can work in the power supply range of l.9V to 4.6V and the ambient temperature of −40°C~+125°C, and has a very fast start-up speed. After digital trimming, the frequency can be adjusted back to the target frequency under the other four process corners, and the circuit supports complete shutdown. Spectre simulation was made based on CSMC’s $0.18\mu \mathrm{m}$ CMOS technology. The final die size is $194\mu \mathrm{m}\times 87\mu \mathrm{m}$.

articleTitle: Design of Quadrature Output Two-stage Differential Ring VCO
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: A 3.8GHz ring oscillator with the two-stage differential structure for PLL is presented. The circuit includes three parts: control voltage-current conversion unit, ring oscillator, and output buffer: control voltage-current conversion unit uses low-threshold transistors to increase the tuning range of the oscillator; to optimize the phase noise of the oscillator, a positive feedback mechanism is introduced into the delay cell, improve the rising and falling speed of the circuit waveform; the output buffer shapes the oscillator output waveform so that the output waveform reaches the rail-to-rail output swing. The simulation results show that the tuning range of the oscillator is 110MHz~7.5GHz, the gain is 6.06GHz/V, the phase noise at 3.8GHz frequency is -94.9dBc/Hz@1MHz, and the power consumption is 7. 56mW.

articleTitle: A 3-Tap Swing-Enhanced Feed-Forward Equalizer
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: A 3-tap feed-forward equalizer based on the TSMC 22nm CMOS process was designed. The feed-forward equalizer consists mainly of delay module, adder module, and tap coefficient control module. The delay module in this design uses latches to implement the delay function. The adder uses a voltage-mode structure. An impedance calibration unit has been designed to calibrate the impedance of the individual driver modules, and a swing enhancement module has been designed for the maximum output swing so that the maximum output swing can be switched between 462mV and 656mV. The tap coefficient control module controls the number of de-emphasis steps in the equalizer, with an equalization range of 0 to 11.5dB. Simulation results show that the differential output eye height is 436mV, jitter is 5.89ps and power consumption is 45.8mW at 0.9 and 1.8V supply voltage.

articleTitle: Cryogenic Measurement of CMOS Readout Circuit Integrated with Silicon-based Blocked-Impurity-Band Detector
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This article proposes a readout integrated circuit (ROIC) for the blocked-impurity-band (BIB) Terahertz (THz) detector, which is operated in the cryogenic (≤6K) environment. This ROIC was designed based on a cryogenic PDK model and used the capacitance trans-impedance amplifier (CTIA) as the input stage. The circuit chip integrated with BIB detector chip was measured at 6K temperature, which avoided the freezing-out effect or kink effect and work normally. The linearity of the chip reaches 97.7%, and the injection efficiency is higher than 95%. Our results provide a potential CMOS readout circuit, which can be used for the cryogenic detector like BIB and other kind of cryogenic device.

articleTitle: A One-Point Trimmed 0.14-mK-Resolution Temperature Sensor Based on Improved Dynamic Element Matching Techniques
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper represents a systematic design of BJT-based temperature sensor with an ultra-high resolution. The system consists of BJT transistors as the sensing elements, a sigma-delta analog-to-digital converter (ADC) which achieves an SNDR of 134 dB and a sigma-delta digital-to-analog converter (DAC) as the trimming module. Dynamic element matching (DEM) techniques are employed to increase the sensing accuracy in the existence of random process variations. Clocking schemes for DEM and trimming subsystems are discussed, which plays a vital role in the achieved dynamic range of the sensor system. The presented work shows that the behavioral model achieves a temperature sensing resolution of 0.14-mK and an inaccuracy of 0.015°.

articleTitle: Research on Microelectronic System of Antagonism Inhibiting Spasticity Based on Electro-Myo-Graphic Bridge
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In this paper, based on the principle of stimulating antagonistic muscles, functional electrical stimulation (FES) is used to achieve the purpose of spasticity suppression. The microelectronic system for spasticity suppression was designed and studied, and then used to simulated spasticity of healthy people. First, based on the characteristics of spastic EMG signals, obtained by the EMG signal detection system of the research group, a detection module was designed to detect EMG signals of voluntary movement, simulated EMG signals of spastic patients. Furthermore, an adaptive pattern recognition algorithm for spasticity was designed to identify spasticity signals from the detected EMG signals. Then, on basis of the functional electrical stimulation core circuit of the research group, a microelectronic FES system based on the myoelectric bridge was designed. Finally, the functional verification experiment of the FES system to stimulate antagonist muscle to inhibit spasm was carried out, The results show that the system is effective for stimulating the wrist extensor muscle as an antagonist muscle to inhibit spasm.

articleTitle: Track-and-Hold Techniques for Ultra High Speed Time-Interleaved ADCs
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: A hierarchical time-interleaved (TI) track-and-hold (T&H) circuit for an ultra high speed analog-to-digital converter (ADC) is presented. The circuit is designed as a frontend for an 8b32GS/s16-way time-interleaved analog-to-digital converters (ADCs) using a 40nm CMOS process. The input and output buffers of the sampled signals are designed in response to the demand of time-interleaving, and the output buffer is a PMOS source-following structure with common mode compensation in order to balance the requirements of bandwidth and common mode. The circuit has an ENOB of S.77 bits and an SFDR of 55.86 dB at the Nyquist input frequency.

articleTitle: Design of Broadband Directional Coupler Based on Wiggly Line Structures
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In this paper, the design of a broadband 5G (the fifth-generation) microstrip directional coupler is presented. This design adopts parallel coupling line structure based on regular wiggly line structure. The advantage of the wiggly line structure is the ability of increasing the coupling capacitance of parallel coupling line structure, achieve good impedance matching and greatly increase the working bandwidth of the directional coupler. Meanwhile, equivalent circuit is presented for the first time to describe its working principle. Adjusting the bending angle of the wiggly line can change the coupling capacitance and increase the degree of freedom, so as to obtain the best coupling capacitance to make a microstrip directional coupler with ultra-wideband, low insertion loss and miniaturization. Measured results show that return loss is more than 22 dB, port isolation is more than 25 dB, Insertion loss is less than 0.6 dB, therefore, the proposed design could provide a promising solution for 5G wireless communication systems. In order to verify the design, a broadband directional coupler in the frequency band of 2.3 – 5 GHz is simulated and designed by using the wiggly line structure, and the electromagnetic simulation software HFSS.

articleTitle: A Low-Noise High-Robust LC-VCO Based on 22nm FD-SOI Process
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: A low-noise LC voltage-controlled oscillator (LC-VCO) based on 22-nm fully depleted silicon on insulator (FD-SOI) process is proposed. The presented 24-GHz LC-VCO with a tuning range of 23.1-25.9 GHz achieves the phase noise of −102 dBc/Hz at 5-MHz offset frequency. And the VCO has high robustness with more than 57% and 28% optimization on the current and trans-conductance (g<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</inf>) deviations, under the process / voltage / temperature (PVT) variations, respectively. The high robustness is ensured by using a back-gate adjustment scheme with the match design between bias circuit and VCO core. The phase noise with 24 dBc/Hz improvement is conducted by employing a LC series resonant cavity to suppress the second-order harmonic. The VCO consumes the power of 20 mW from a supply voltage of 0.8 V.

articleTitle: A 28GHz Doherty Power Amplifier MMIC for 5G Millimeter Band Communication
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In this paper, a 28GHz Doherty power amplifier for 5G communication is presented in a 0.15-$\mu$m depletion mode (D-mode) Gallium Arsenide (GaAs) pHEMT from Win’s corporation. To simplify the impedance transformations both in output power back-off region and at saturation, the compensation line behind the main power amplifier is removed without degrading the back-off efficiency by choosing an appropriate output matching network. Electromagnetic (EM) simulated results show that the saturation output power and power added-efficiency (PAE) of the proposed Doherty power amplifier are better than 27dBm and 37% respectively in the frequency band of 27.5 GHz -28.5 GHz. The PAE at 6 dB output power back-off are obtained as 30.5% $\sim$31.3%, and the chip size is 3.2mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</sup> 1.6mm.

articleTitle: Tracing Security Verification Based on Logic Conformance for IP-Based Design
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: With the rapid development of IP core technology, it is necessary to study the security of IP core in circuit design. IP core can be divided into Soft Core, Hard Core, and Firm Core. Most of the existing methods are used to verify the Soft core, and few methods that can verify the security of the Solid core and Hard core. Therefore, this paper combines the formal methods with functional simulation and proposes a method of tracing security verification based on logic conformance. This method based on logic conformance can abstract and simplify the circuit structure. Then the security verification method of tracing security verification is used to test, simulation and verify the security problem of IP core. Finally, this paper builds the actual RSA circuit model. The results of simulation confirm that the method can effectively detect the security problems in the IP core.

articleTitle: Low-Power Dynamic Comparator with Complementary Push-Pull Pre-amplifier For Pipelined ADCs
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In order to adapt to the usage scenario of low power consumption of the Internet of Things (IoT) and meet the working requirements of low power supply voltage and low input common mode voltage, analog-to-digital converters (ADCs) are continuously being pushed to their performance limits and have seen tremendous decrease in their power consumption in the past few years. This paper presents a low-power, low-offset, and high-speed dynamic comparator for a GS/s pipelined ADC consisting of a complementary push-pull based pre-amplifier and a cross-coupled pair-based latch, which increases bandwidth and reduces offset as well as signal kickback. The pre-amplifier achieves a DC gain of 17.16dB and a bandwidth of 6.81GHz, making the overall comparator bandwidth of 6.15GHz, and the flip time of the latch is 25.5ps. Through 1000 times of Monte Carlo analysis, the standard deviation $\sigma$ of the comparator offset is 6.988mv, which meets the overall system design requirements. The presented dynamic comparator occupies an active area of 60.91$\mu$m2 in 28 nm process, while consuming 0.58mW at 0.9V.

articleTitle: Calibration Study on Noise Figure Measurement with Precision Attenuator Method
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: The new improved approach for noise Figure are introduced in terms of the signal analysis and two terminal theory. Compared with the traditional method, it is convenient to improve the mismatch problem and reflection effects of NF analyzer over a wide range of frequency. Firstly, it’s revealed that the precision attenuators have the significant advantage of low VSWR and wide bandwidth. Furthermore, the appropriate calibration method provides the suitable formulation for the measurement accuracy and the minimize mismatch uncertainty. Eventually, it’s shown that the evaluation of uncertainty measurement is proposed.

articleTitle: Design Analysis of Wideband 24-40GHz GaN-on-Si SPDT Switches for 5G Millimeter-Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Microwave switch design analysis using a 100 nm GaN-on-Si high-electron-mobility transistors (HEMTs) technology is discussed in this letter. Analyzed semi-quantitatively, the switch turn-on and turn-off channels are treated as Butterworth-type filters to better realize insertion loss (IL) and isolation optimization with the given bandwidth. An extra open-circuit transmission line is adopted in the input port to ensure better input impedance matching. As experimental vehicles for the presented analysis, two wideband high-power single-pole double-throw switches employing three-and four-shunt HEMTs were implemented separately for fifth generation millimeter-wave applications. Measurement results for these two cases demonstrate state-of-the-art IL of less than 1.4/1.65 dB and isolations of better than 28/34 dB for the wideband frequency range of 24-40 GHz.

articleTitle: Research on Glitch Power Estimation of Combinational Logic Circuits
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Aiming at the problem that glitch power consumption is ignorant when evaluating power consumption at the earlier stage, especially at register-transfer-level, this paper proposes a method to estimate the glitch at the logic synthesis stage. This method analyzes the factors affecting the glitch and creates a prediction model based on the simulation data of the glitch and the random forest regression algorithm. The experimental results show that the error of the glitch prediction is within 20% at the logic synthesis stage.

articleTitle: A 1532 nm laser-excited NaLuF₄:Er³⁺, Ho³⁺ material for thermometer
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: The high concentration of trivalent lanthanum ions doping upconversion (UC) luminescent materials will cause a concentration quenching phenomenon, resulting in low luminous efficiency. In this work, The addition of Ho<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup> ions to NaLuF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>:20% Er<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup> crystals can effectively enhance the UC emission. Especially the red light is significantly enhanced. The optical temperature dependence of Er<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup> ions is investigated based on fluorescence intensity ratios (FIR) from non-thermally coupled levels (NTCLs) <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup> S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3/2</inf>, <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup> F<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">9/2</inf> and <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup> S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3/2</inf>, <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup> I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">9/2</inf>. The sensitivity (S) of NaLuF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>:Er<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup>/Ho<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup> based materials reached 0. $624-1.556\mathrm{K}^{-1}$ in the 293 - 570 K temperature interval. The results show that the NaLuF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>:Er<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup>/Ho<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup> material can be used in high-precision optical thermometers.

articleTitle: A Delay Matching Technique for Relative Deterministic Jitter Reduction in 28GHz ADPLL
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: A technique for relative deterministic jitter (DJ) reduction in 28GHz all digital phase-locked loops (ADPLL) is proposed. The reference clock path and feedback clock path of the ADPLL are optimized in 28nm CMOS Technology, especially for CML-to-CMOS circuit, and a delay matching technique is realized to reduce the relative DJ caused by power supply noise between the two input signals of the phase frequency detector (PFD). The frequency of reference clock is 250MHz, while the output clock of ADPLL is 28GHz. The simulation results show that the relative DJ between the two input signals of the PFD is reduced from 1.71ps to 110fs after delay matching.

articleTitle: A 14-bit 500-MS/s Pipelined-SAR ADC in 28-nm CMOS with Foreground and Background Calibration
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: A 14-bit 500-MS/s Pipelined-SAR (Successive Approximation Register) Analog-to-Digital Converter (ADC) in 2S-nm CMOS is presented in this paper. The ADC has two-stages. In the first stage, Multi-comparators are used to increase the speed of ADC. A foreground calibration method for capacitor mismatch and a background calibration method for gain mismatch are implemented. This design also optimizes the processing logic of the capacitor foreground calibration to increase the speed of the chip. In the second stage, two SAR ADCs basing on Time-Interleaved (TI) method are used to achieve the required sampling rate. The results reveal that the ADC achieves a 64.36 dB SNDR and 73.29 dB SFDR at 500-MS/s sampling rate without calibration, 66.19 dB SNDR and 83.50 dB SFDR at 500-MS/s sampling rate with calibration. The layout of core occupies 0.43 mm2 area and consumes 215.6 mW at 2.0/1.0 V supplies.

articleTitle: A high-Speed CAN Bus Transmitter with Low Electromagnetic Emission
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: CAN (Controller Area Network) bus transceivers have high requirements for security and performance, which are mainly used in automotive networks, machine automation and other fields,. This paper designs and implements a high-speed CAN bus transmitter with low electromagnetic emission (EME). The slew rate of the output signal is reduced by successively controlling the switching of the transistor at the output end of the transmitter, and a negative feedback structure that can balance the current capability of the output power transistor is used to improve signal symmetry. The chip is designed based on 60V 0.18$\mu$ m BCD process. The test results show that at the transmission rate of 5Mbit/s, the output of the transmitter complies with the explicit and implicit requirements of the CAN bus level, the output common mode signal has good voltage symmetry, and the average value of the common mode FFT is 66.26dB, which can be applied to high in highly reliable CAN transceivers.

articleTitle: A design of High-linearity Blocker Tolerant RF Receiver Based on Four-Path Filter
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: A blocker tolerant RF receiver based on four-path filter is proposed, which aims to achieve high linearity and low power consumption. Differential structure allows for switch sharing which halves the effective resistance to reduce drain-source voltage modulation. The two input differential signals pass through the first stage voltage input voltage output filter (V-V BPF) and the second stage voltage input current output filter (V-I BPF) respectively in the RF domain. Its equivalent RLC model is realized by using the four path filter structure based on MOSFET, so the two-stage cascaded BPF will achieve good blocker suppression effect. The signal passing through the two-stage BPF will be converted down and through the passive mixer, then base band signal will be output. Finally, the two-stage TIA in the base band domain (BB domain) is used to amplify the base band signal, so as to output two in band differential signals $\mathrm{VO}\_{}\mathrm{I}$ and $\mathrm{VO}\_{}\mathrm{Q}$ with good signal-to-noise ratio for subsequent processing. Using tsmcN65 technology, it can achieve IIP3 of +37.7dBm for a blocker frequency offset of 80MHz, consumes 47.7-57.2mW for 0.5-2GHz LO and occupies an area of 0.17 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: A Blocker-Tolerant Mixer-First Receiver with Channel BW Extention Technique Achieving 22.2 dBm OOB-IIP3 and 23.3 MHz BW
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In this work, a 0.5-to-2 GHz blocker-tolerant mixer-first receiver (RX) is proposed, which features a pair of complex poles to extend the Bandwidth (BW) and enhance the linearity, a fully-differential low-noise transconductance-amplifier (LNTA) to improve noise Figure (NF), and a transmission-gate (TG) mixer to reduce the local oscillator (LO) leakage. By using an attenuator as the bypass feedback of capacitor, a pair of complex poles is introduced at baseband (BB) as low-pass response and frequency-translated to RF as bandpass response, achieving −40dB/dec roll-off slope. When implemented in 65 nm CMOS technology, the simulation results show that at 80 MHz offset the RX achieves 22.2 dBm OOB-IIP3, 23.3 MHz channel BW and −81 dBm LO leakage. Covering from 0.5 to 2 GHz, the NF ranges 4.1 to 6.2 dB while the RX consumes a reasonable power of 57 to 75 mW. The active area is $0.96 mm^{2}$.

articleTitle: Adaptive Slope Compensation for Improving Load Capability
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: It is excessive or insufficient slope compensation current in buck DC-DC converters that cause available load current reduction and subharmonic oscillation issues. In this paper, a slope compensation circuit scheme was proposed, concerned with the input/output voltage changes and the product of the inductor current and the on-resistance of the power transistor. Compared with the traditional adaptive slope compensation circuit, the proposed circuit includes the influence factor of the power transistor on-resistance and demonstrates its slope compensation relationship, based on which an adaptive slope compensation circuit with Flip Voltage Fllower (FVF) structure is formed. Finally, the self-regulation and precise controlling of compensation amount can be achieved. The load capability and transient response of the DC-DC converter is improved and thus the system stability can be guaranteed. Experimental results show that the maximum inductor current change is less than 12% with the duty cycle ranging from 11% to 73%.

articleTitle: A Clock Delivery Path with Peaking Buffers for 112Gb/s Wireline Transceiver
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: With the ever-increasing demand of higher wireline data rates in recent years, long-range on-chip clock delivery for multiple transceivers (TRX) is underway, in which DC offset is accumulated through multistage clock buffers, causing quadrature error and inducing deterministic jitter that degrades bit error rate. This paper presents a clock delivery path design for 112Gb/s wireline transceivers, in which peaking buffers suppress DC offset to realize lower quadrature error. Remaining error is then dealt with by capacitor-DAC based quadrature-error canceller (QEC). Implemented in 28nm CMOS process, the quadrature error in proposed clock path achieves a standard deviation of 1.61°. The QEC provides a +/−6.55° tuning range with a step of 0.94°.

articleTitle: A 9-bit 500-MS/s 2-then-1b/cycle SAR ADC with Dynamic Background Offset Calibration Technique
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper presents a low power asynchronous 9-bit 500-MS/s 2-then-1b/cycle successive approximation register (SAR) ADC in 40-nm CMOS technology. The proposed efficient ADC shows good performance against offset mismatch of the comparator array by background calibration technique. The operation of the proposed background calibration module does not depend on the input signal distribution by quantizing the same residue signal in the last 1b/cycle phase. This module which is turned on dynamically without extra comparison phase can reduce conversion time. A majority vote logic is also introduced to improve the effective number of bits (ENOB) of the ADC. The calibration enhances SFDR from 61.63 dB to 68.7 dB, ENOB from 7.57 bits to 8.79 bits, SNDR from 47.38 dB to 54.7 dB for a near-Nyquist input. The proposed SAR ADC consumes 2.11mW under 1.1V supply with Walden Figure of merit (FOM) of 9.27 fJ/conversion-step.

articleTitle: A General-Purpose CNN Accelerator Based on Improved Systolic Array for FPGAs
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In recent years, convolutional neural networks have been increasingly used for processing image tasks, such as target recognition, image enhancement, and other areas. In the embedded and IoT fields, the small size and low-power application characteristics make it impractical to deploy high-performance computing devices on hardware platforms in this field. In this paper, a general neural network accelerator is designed that can be scaled to any size, which can be adapted to hardware platforms in different application areas including data centers and IoT according to power consumption and arithmetic power requirements. The accelerator is based on the improved systolic array, which improves the utilization and throughput of data and reduces the system power consumption. This paper uses int8 data type to match embedded and IoT low-power requirements. In this paper, the accelerator is deployed on the XC7Z020 hardware platform, compared with CPU and GPU platforms, and evaluate the performance of handwritten digit recognition neural network based on the Minist dataset. The experimental results show that the energy consumption ratio of the design in this paper is 10 times better compared to current advanced CPUs and GPUs, and more than 300 times better compared to current CPUs in the embedded domain.

articleTitle: PMBVD Model Parameter Extraction and Optimization for Film Bulk Acoustic Resonator
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This work builds a Modified Mason model and extracts the parameters of the Parasitic Modified Butterworth-Van Dyke(PMBVD) from the resonance curves, which can simulate the impedance characteristics of Film Bulk Acoustic Resonator(FBAR) in the full waveband more accurately. By including the effective area of the support layer and the effective area of electrode into the model, as well as adding parasitic capacitance, inductance and resistance introduced by packaging, the extracted resonance curves can provide a more accurate representation of the impedance characteristics and Q-value of the resonator near the resonance point, making it easier to fit to the test parameters. After the extraction, Yield Analysis performed to demonstrate the accuracy of the extracted parameters. By demonstrating excellent agreement between the extracted parameters and the measurement data, the PMBVD model developed in this work provides a more accurate guideline for 5G filter design.

articleTitle: DC–DC Buck Converter Using Equivalent Inductance for Advanced Phase Technology
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In the traditional Buck-type chip, low ESR capacitance is usually used to reduce the output ripple of switching power supply, which also affects the feedback loop, making the zero point of LC network far away from the traverse frequency, resulting in the phase lag of the system. In this paper, based on the Type-II compensation network, the advanced phase technology is used to compensate the phase near the unit bandwidth, so that the chip is prepared in advance to solve the problem of phase lag. But the inductor is not easy to be integrated in the chip, so the equivalent inductor is used to realize the advanced phase technology. Simplis software is used in this paper to model the loop, and Cadence software is used to simulate and verify the circuit based on CSMC 0.25$\mu$ m BCD process. The simulation results show that the phase margin provided by the advanced phase technology for the system is 45°.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of 5.8 GHz Rectifier Antenna
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Wireless power transmission (WPT) system have a wide range of applications in many fields such as science, military, industry, and medicine. Rectifier antennas and arrays are one of the key technologies of WPT systems. This paper focuses on a Schottky diode-based C-band (5.8 GHz) microstrip rectifier antenna, in which the rectifier circuit can obtain the best RF-DC conversion efficiency of 64% and DC output voltage of 2.75 V at an input power of 20 dBm. Meanwhile, the RF-DC conversion efficiency of more than 33% can be achieved in the input power range of 5 dBm-22 dBm. The receiving antenna has harmonic suppression and is in microstrip form, forming a 4x4 square array to complete the reception of C-band signals. The maximum gain of the antenna array is 18. 16dBic and the normal axis ratio is 1. 62dB. This rectifier antenna has the advantages of low cost, simple structure and easy array, which has the potential to be applied in the field of WPT.

articleTitle: Integrating Tetrahydrofurfuryl Methacrylate onto Perovskite Surface for High Stability Perovskite Solar Cells
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Organic-inorganic metal halide perovskite materials have attracted extensive attention owing to their outstanding optoelectronic characteristics. One-step spin coating with antisolvent proved to be an efficient method for preparing perovskite films in small-area devices. For environmental reasons, it is worth advocating for avoiding the introduction of non-environmentally friendly antisolvents in the preparation of perovskite films. Our work prepared high-quality perovskite films by vacuum quenching assisted spin-coating without antisolvent. To further improve the hydrophobicity of the perovskite surface, a light-cured cross-linking tetrahydrofurfuryl methacrylate (THFMA) molecule was selected to realize the inner encapsulation of perovskite films. Based on the internal packaging strategy, the champion perovskite solar cell significantly improves the device efficiency and stability compared with unmodified devices. The champion perovskite solar cell stored in the air for 30 days still preserved more than 85% of the original device’s efficiency. Finally, we confirmed that the polymerized tetrahydrofurfuryl methacrylate layer not only passivates the surface defects of perovskite films but also enhances the hydrophobicity.

articleTitle: A Low-Power Blocker-Tolerant Receiver with Wideband Negative-Feedback Technique Achieving 22.4dBm OOB-IIP3
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper proposes a low-power four-phase wideband negative-feedback (WNF) receiver which is tunable to operate at 0.1 to 2GHz. A gain-boosted N-path low-noise amplifier (LNA) is employed to achieve both low noise Figure (NF) and high linearity. Besides, an extra up-conversion path is introduced from baseband (BB) output to radio frequency (RF) input to create a negative-feedback loop that optimizes the input-impedance matching. The Miller theory has been extended to passive-mixer switches to realize a smaller input parasitic capacitance. Implemented in 65nm CMOS process, the simulation results show that the receiver achieves 22.4dBm OOB-IIP3 at 80MHz offset frequency and 16.4MHz channel BW at 2GHz. When covering 0.1 to 2GHz, the NF ranges from 2.S to 5dB and gain varies from 31.8 to 35.7dB, while only paying 7 to 31mW power consumption.

articleTitle: Ripple Compensation Based On COT Control Mode
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In the traditional Constant-On-Time (COT) control mode, the output bypass capacitor mostly uses ceramic capacitors, and its equivalent series resistance (ESR) is small, the phase of output voltage ripple lags behind the inductor current, causing system instability. For this reason, this paper adopts the ripple compensation technology. By injecting the external ramp and the internal inductor current ramp, a virtual resistance is introduced for the ESR, and the resistance value of the ESR is increased to meet the stability conditions. The chip is designed based on 18V 0.1Sum BCD process. The simulation results show that when the input voltage is 12V and the temperature is 27°C, the system conversion efficiency can reach 97%, and the system output voltage ripple is about 3.4mV.

articleTitle: A 25% Duty -Cycle Clock Generation Circuit in 0.13 μ m CMOS
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: A 25% duty cycle clock generation circuit for wireless transceiver is designed in this paper, including divider based on current mode logic (CML) latch, the AND gates and buffers. The advantages and disadvantages of main structure and the principle of the clock generation circuit are analyzed. The key sub-circuits and layouts such as the divider-by-two, logic gates and buffers are designed based on 0.13μ m CMOS process. The simulation results show that the operating frequency range of the 25% duty cycle clock generation circuit is 0.02-2.5GHz, and the rise (fall) time is 0.02-ns.

articleTitle: A Heterogeneous RISC-V SoC for Confidential Computing and Password Recovery
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In today’s silicon design, there are far more processors than the main ones. Domain-specific accelerators and coprocessors are widely used to continuing to increase the performance and energy efficiency of computing systems. Focused on the security domain, this paper presents a heterogeneous ASIC SoC built with the most popular open-source RISC-V ISA, a coprocessor providing the trusted execution environment for confidential computing and an energy efficient rule-based password generation accelerator. Thanks to its continuously completing ecosystem, the RISC-V core provides application interfaces and task management for the whole SoC, through which we validated the security mechanism for confidential computing in the coprocessor and tested the performance of the password generation accelerator. In addition to verifying the functionality of our design in GlobalFoundries 22FDX technology, the evaluation results also show that our password recovery system is able to process about 0.97 passwords per cycle at 500 MHz and is $25.4 \times$ more energy efficient than that of FPGA implementation.

articleTitle: An Adaptive Daul Step Control Dead-Time Circuit for Gallium Nitride Half-Bridge
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In order to reasonably design the dead time and reduce the ineffective energy consumptions of the circuit in the dead time, an adaptive dual-step control dead time circuit suitable for GaN(gallium nitride) half-bridge structure is proposed. The circuit mainly detects the when the voltage of the switch node drops to the bias voltage by detecting the falling edge, skips the time that causes the shoot-through loss by designing the corresponding time delay, and then detects the negative voltage of the switch node and outputs an effective output Logic level, carry out digital feedback to the capacitor array unit, effectively control the capacitor array to perform dynamic dead time delay, use digital control to continuously adjust the dead time, so that the dead time can achieve the optimal result, reducing the system power consumption in dead time, improving system performance. This circuit is based on a standard 0.35μm BCD (Bipolar-CMOSDMOS) process and 40V LD-MOS(Laterally Diffused Metal-Oxide Semiconductor)high voltage devices, and the dead zone control circuit is verified at a frequency of 1 Mhz. The results show that when the input voltage is 40V and the load current is 26.67mA, the negative voltage feedback judgment output is input to the reversible counter continuously switches between 0010 and 0011 for dynamic time delay, so that the dead time is near the ideal time, the dynamic delay time of 0010 is 5.87ns, and the state delay of 0011 the time is 7.10ns, and the dynamic adjustment step is about 1.23ns, compared with the traditional fixed dead time, the efficiency is improved by about 3%.

articleTitle: Research and Implementation of ONU Data Synchronization Circuit in 100G EPON System
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Aiming at the continuous stream synchronization of the ONU (Optical Network Unit) in the 100G EPON system, this paper proposes a mathematical model for judging the synchronization threshold. Based on the proposed threshold mathematical model, the optimal synchronization scheme is selected, and the ONU continuous bitstream synchronization circuit in 100G EPON system is designed, and the feasibility and stability of the designed circuit are analyzed. In this paper, the continuous bit stream synchronization circuit on ONU side is simulated to ensure that the function of the synchronization circuit is correct. Stratix10 1SD280PT2F55E1VG chip was used to complete the hardware test of the synchronous circuit. Finally, the test data are analyzed and summarized, and the decision threshold of synchronous circuit is given precisely. The results show that the synchronization circuit designed in this paper has good stability and can meet the synchronization index of 100G EPON system.

articleTitle: Adaptive Ramp Generator for CMOS Image Sensor
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: The system resolution of a CMOS image sensor (CIS) is determined by the resolution of an internal single-slope analog-to-digital(SS ADC) converter. The structure of a single-slope ADC is usually composed of a comparator, a ramp generator, a decoder, and a register. The traditional integrated ramp generator circuit is greatly affected by process, voltage and temperature, which results in low accuracy and poor linearity of the ramp signal. This paper introduces a ramp generator which can adjust the slope adaptively. On the basis of the integral ramp generator, the negative feedback mechanism is achieved by the pulse-width locked loop (PWLL) circuit structure. The designed pulse-width locked loop circuit consists of a phase detector, a charge pump and a pulse width modulator. The DNL of the adaptive ramp generator is −0.00054LSB/+0.00033LSB and the INL is −0.00054LSB/+1.103808LSB, which indicates that the structure can adjust the ramp signal dynamically and improve the anti-PVT capability of the ramp signal. Compared with the ramp generator in the references, the ramp in this paper has the advantages of high accuracy and low power consumption.

articleTitle: Multi-peak Vector Synthesis Gain Equalizer
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper proposes a new multi-peak vector synthesis gain equalizer which is different from the traditional resonant gain equalizer. The equalizer utilizes a multi-stage Wilkinson power splitter to achieve multiple outputs of unequal amplitude, which produce a phase difference after passing through a phase delay line and then vector synthesis by the power splitter, where electromagnetic waves of opposite phase superimpose destructively and those of the same phase superimpose constructively. This equalizer has a compact size, flexible adjustability and can realize complex equalization curves. The gain equalizer has equalization value of 7. 4dB at 29. 5GHz and 6dB at 35.1GHz on the Ka band with the minimum insertion loss (IL) of 3dB and a return loss better than 10dB.

articleTitle: Design of a 5MHz 4A Half Bridge Gate Driver in 180nm BCD Process for GaN HEMT
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: A half-bridge gate driver for enhanced-mode GaN HEMT is designed. In order to improve the speed, a new high voltage level-shift circuit is designed. The level-shift circuit uses a variety of strategies to reduce transmission delay, including a common-mode noise cancellation circuit and a positive feedback interlock circuit without RC filtering. Based on the proposed high voltage level-shift circuit, a 5MHz half-bridge gate driver chip with a current of 4A and an output voltage of 6V is implemented in the 180nm BCD process. The test results show that the prototype gate driver has a rise time of 4.1ns and a fall time of 3. 8ns at 5MHz switching frequency for 3nF load. This meets the gate driver requirements of GaN HEMT.

articleTitle: Two-Step Single-Slope ADC with Three-Stage Bandwidth-Limited Comparator for CMOS Image Sensors
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper proposes a low-power column parallel two-step single-slope Analog-to-Digital Converter (SS ADC) with three-stage Bandwidth-Limited preamplifier. The slight expanding ramp generator is used to reduce the accuracy error caused by the limited bandwidth. A prototype sensor was designed using UMC 110 nm CMOS image sensors process. The simulation results show that the proposed three-stage Bandwidth-Limited preamplifier consumes $73\mu\mathrm{W}$ power per column, saved 70% power consumption. The DNL is −0.2LSB/ +0.4LSB, INL is −0.2LSB/ +0.3LSB at 20MHz with 3.3V/1.2V supply voltage.

articleTitle: A 10-bit 1-MS/s Low-Power SAR ADC with an Integrated Buffer in Dual Sample-and-Hold Architecture
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper presents a low-power design of a 10-bit successive approximation register (SAR) analog-to-digital converter (ADC) with an integrated buffer. A dual sample-and-hold architecture is employed which significantly extends the sampling time. For the same settling accuracy, the GBW of the input buffer dramatically decreases leading to the reduction of power consumption by 90% compared to the conventional sampling schemes. The system is fabricated in a 0.18 μm CMOS process and operates under a 1.8-V supply. The ADC achieves an ENOB of 9.45 bits at 1 MS/s sampling rate and consumes 261.7 μW including the peripheral buffer.

articleTitle: An Encoder Design for High-Speed Pipelined Folding-Interpolation ADC
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: The paper presents the design of an encoder for high-speed pipelined folding-interpolation (F/I) analog-to-digital converter (ADC). The encoder adopts coarse-fine bit cooperative coding mode, has error-correcting coding function, allows zero-crossing offset, can judge overflow, and is convenient to expand in accuracy. It is suitable for high-speed and high precision pipelined cascaded F/IADC. At the high sampling rate of 1.6GSPS, the single-core ADC in this encoder can achieve an effective resolution of 10.39 bit and an SFDR of 82.6dBc.

articleTitle: Inductively-Coupled High-Speed Interconnects of 3D-Integrated CMOS Image Sensors
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper presents a high-speed interconnect of 3D-integrated backside-illuminated (BSI) CMOS image Sensor (CIS) chip by inductive coupling link. With the CIS fusion oxide bonding process, the two stacked chips are able to be planted face to face, reducing the interconnect distance to 5um, which benefits for diminishing the channel insertion loss through inductive coupling. With a proper impedance matching network, the simulated insertion loss of the inductive coupling channel can be as low as -1.1dB. Schemes of inductive coupling links, either with or without carrier waves are compared. A $4 \times 4$ coupling array enables a data rate of 80Gb/s (5Gb/s per channel), corresponding to an area efficiency of 270Gbs/mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. This scheme offers a realizable low-cost high-speed solution for BSI-CIS 3D integration.

articleTitle: A 28Gb/s NRZ and 56Gb/s PAM4 SerDes Dual-Mode Transmitters Based on 28nm CMOS
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper designs a dual-mode transmitter that supports non-return to-zero modulation (NRZ) at a rate of 28 Gb/s and four-level pulse amplitude modulation (PAM4) at a rate of 56Gb/s, using CMOS 28nm process. The transmitter uses a 4:1MUX with a 1/2 speed architecture to reduce the transmitter area. CML2CMOS circuit is used to convert the signal into a full swing signal. The design of the clock buffer circuit improves the driving ability. The output 56Gb/s PAM4 call consumes 265mW and the energy efficiency is 4.7pJ/bit. The 28GB /s NRZ signal consumes 215mW and the energy efficiency is 7.6pJ/bit.

articleTitle: Fast Start Low Power DC-DC Conversion Circuit Design
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: A fast-start low-power DC-DC conversion circuit is designed. The conversion circuit adopts two charging methods: direct charging and charge pump charging, which greatly shortens the time for the output voltage to reach a stable value, thereby achieving the function of fast start-up. A high-frequency oscillator is used to reduce the output voltage ripple, and at the same time, the output voltage is indirectly detected to reduce power consumption. The circuit has completed the design and layout design of the conversion circuit. The chip simulation results indicate that under the 3V voltage source, the conversion circuit can shorten the charging time by 22% compared with the single charge pump charging method. At the same time, the working current of the comparator module in the circuit is reduced from 9.13uA to 334nA, and the overall operating current of the circuit is decreased from 30.2uA to 23.5uA.

articleTitle: A Ku-Band Power Amplifier with 13dBm OP1dB in 40-nm CMOS
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper presents a high linearity and broadband Ku-Band power amplifier (PA) in 40-nm CMOS process. On-chip transformers are used in the matching networks to provide optimum load impedance and achieve broadband matching. A two-stage PA is proposed for higher gain and output power. Neutralization capacitance is used for both stages to compensate the feedback effect due to the gate-drain parasitic capacitance CGD. The design and layout of the Driver stage and Output stage are optimized to achieve both high output power and gain. To improve both linearity and efficiency, transistors of the Output stage are biased in deep class-AB. The simulation results demonstrate that the PA chip achieves a saturated output power of 16.8-dBm, a $\mathrm{P}\mathrm{A}\mathrm{E}_{\max}$ of 24.5% and a 14.5-dBm $\mathrm{O}\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{1}\mathrm{d}\mathrm{B}}$ with a maximum power gain of 25.5-dB. The chip area including all pads is 0.37 $\mathrm{m}\mathrm{m}^{2}$.

articleTitle: A 6bit Ultra-Wideband Passive Phase Shifter in 0.13μm BiCMOS Technology
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In this paper, a 6-18GHz ultra-wideband passive vector modulator phase shifter is proposed based on $0.13\mu \mathrm{m}$ BiCMOS technology. A transformer-based quadrature signal poly-phase network is used to generate high precision quadrature signals over the whole band, the quadrature signals are scaled by a digitally controlled transistor array, then combined for phase interpolations to in the range of 0-360°. The proposed passive vector modulator phase shifter can perform phase shifting in the range of 360° by 5.625° step. The results indicate that the maximum RMS phase error is 2.7°, and the RMS amplitude error is less than 0.33dB in the range of 6-18GHz.

articleTitle: A Mismatch Error Calibration Method for 14-bit 500MS/s Time-interleaved Charge-Domain ADC
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: A mix-signal type high precision mismatch error calibration method for time-interleaved ADCs is proposed. The calibration method calibrates the clock skew mismatch error based on binary search algorithm. Based on the proposed calibration method, a 14-bit 500MS/s ADC is designed and realized in a 1P6M 0.18 $\mu$m CMOS process. Test results show the 14-bit 500MS/s ADC achieves the SNR of 69.8dBFS and the SFDR of 82.3dB, with 72.1MHz input at 500MS/s, while consumes the power consumption of 365mW.

articleTitle: Broadband Power Amplifier Design in 130nm CMOS
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In this paper, a power amplifier with stacked structure is designed, of which feasibility is analyzed in terms of broadband design and high output power design directions. Subsequently, a two-stage cascaded triple-stacked power amplifier circuit and its layout are designed based on 130-nm CMOS process. The simulation results show that the 3-dB bandwidth of this power amplifier is 1.29-8.65 GHz. The output power exceeds 21-dBm in the range of 2-6 GHz, the power added efficiency(PAE) exceeds 19%. Meanwhile, the power amplifier has positive input and output return loss performance, which is less than −7 dB in the range of 2-6 GHz.

articleTitle: A 4 Gb/s Adaptive CTLE Based on Data Edge Counting and 8B10B Coding for DisplayPort
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper proposes a 4 Gb/s adaptive continuous-time linear equalizer (CTLE) based on data edge counting and 8Bl0B coding for DisplayPort to compensate channel loss and inter-symbol interference (ISI) resulting from limited channel bandwidth. 8Bl0B coding used in DisplayPort guarantees that serialized 8Bl0B encoded data stream has a high transition density between 0 and 1 for clock data recovery and DC-balancing. Taking advantage of this characteristic of 8Bl0B coding, the proposed adaptive CTLE quickly adjusts its peaking gain by counting rising data edges to achieve optimal equalization for a transmission channel with 13-dB loss used in DisplayPort. The proposed adaptive scheme is mainly composed of a programmable CTLE using a negative capacitance circuit, a pipelined 8Bl0B encoder, a pipelined 8Bl0B decoder, a data edge counter and an adaptation controller. The proposed circuit has been designed with a 180 nm CMOS process as part of a DisplayPort transceiver. Simulation results show that the proposed CTLE achieves adaptation in 4 $\mu$s and consumes 10.8 mW from a 1. SV supply.

articleTitle: A Design Study of a Miniaturized Equalizer Based on CSRR Structure
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In this paper, a microstrip equalizer based on a new resonant structure of CSRR is designed by cascading the resonant characteristics of CSRR, loaded on an alumina ceramic substrate. Compared with the conventional dendritic resonator, the resonator of CSRR structure has better capacitive and inductive characteristics and can reduce the circuit size with the same index. Modeled by HFSS simulation, the designed equalizer has a volume of 9. 2mm$\times$ 6mm$\times$ 0.254mm, a maximum equilibrium of 13dB in the 10GHz to 16GHz band, a minimum insertion loss of 0. 9dB, and a return loss better than 11dB. This paper provides a new idea for the design of miniaturized equalizer in low frequency band.

articleTitle: The Circuit Design of a High Precision Forehead Thermometer
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Given the problem that the measurement accuracy of the current market thermometer is not high enough, this thesis aims to design a high-precision thermometer. The thesis analyzes the main factors that affect the accuracy of the infrared temperature sensor measurement results and uses the Kalman filter method to preprocess the data. An error compensation algorithm using MEA-BP neural network algorithm and least square curve fitting is proposed to obtain the measurement results with higher accuracy [1]. The temperature value is displayed through the OLED display module, and voice broadcast, high-temperature alarm, and temperature measurement mode can be set.

articleTitle: An Ultra-Low-Power Wake-up Receiver with an Integrated PUF ID and Programmable Miss-Detection and False-Alarm Rates
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: An ultra-low-power wake-up receiver (WuRx) is presented in this work. The WuRx integrates a 30-bit physically-unclonable-function-based unique ID for independent specification. A programmable correlator based on Hamming distance comparison is proposed for systematic control of the miss-detection rate, RMD, and the false-alarm rate, RFA. Implemented in a 0.18$\mu$m CMOS process, the WuRx operates at 433 MHz and features a data rate of16.384 kbit/s based on on-off keying (OOK) modulation. Simulation results show a sensitivity of −5S.SdBm and a power consumption of 57.33 nW from a 1.6 V supply voltage while achieving both RMD and RFA of less than 0.1%.

articleTitle: Mr_Kru: Accelerator of Kruskal’s Algorithm for Finding Root Node in Parallel
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Minimum Spanning Tree(MST) is widely used in VLSI design, network routing, human brain network analysis and other fields. Kruskal’s algorithm is one of the classical methods to find the minimum spanning tree. Aiming at the problem that the root node search time accounts for a high proportion of the Kruskal’s algorithm, according to the characteristics of real world graph data, this paper presents a hardware accelerator Mr-Kru for the Kruskal’s algorithm to find the root node in parallel based on the Coordinate(COO) compression format. In this paper, the prototype system is built on the Virtex UltraScale+VCU118 evaluation platform, and complete the hardware testing of Mr_Kru based on four different datasets. The experimental results show that the running time of parallel mode is 34.9%~41.6% lower than that of serial mode. The resource cost is 97.6% and 99.6% lower than that of the comparative literature. Vivado simulation power consumption is 2. 671W.

articleTitle: Hardware Data Prefetch for XiangShan Processor
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: XiangShan, a rising star of RISC-V-based processors proposed by Chinese Academy of Science, is famous for its high performance and agile methodology. At present, the second-generation Yanqi Lake architecture of XiangShan has already reached the frequency of 2GHz at the 14nm process node, which ranks the first in the field of open-source RISC-V-based processors. One of the key approaches that contribute to its high performance is prefetch. A timely and accurate prefetcher can effectively eliminate cache misses and thus hide memory access latency. Aiming at the specific environment of XiangShan, out-of-order and parallel, a stride-based prefetcher for the L1DCache is achieved on the Yanqi Lake structure of XiangShan. Serious benchmarks from SPEC2006 were run on XiangShan, the result of which demonstrates that our prefetcher improves the performance of XiangShan by an average of 2.5% and up to 13.3%.

articleTitle: Study on Warpage of Interposer by Chip Distribution
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Glass interposer have gradually become an effective substitute for silicon and ceramic substrates due to their high-frequency performance, excellent electrical isolation, low price, and could be fabricated with large size. However, the warpage for wafer level 2.5D or 3D packaging using glass interposer is a serious issue. This paper studies the warpage caused by thermal mismatch in the packaging process using different modulus and coefficient of thermal expansion(CTE) epoxy resin materials, and explores whether the chip distribution has an effect on the warpage and the change law.The pattern of wafer warpage is explored by controlling a single variable, changing the position of the chip patch and using different CTEs of epoxy resin materials.

articleTitle: Ka-Band LNA Design Using Systematic Circuit Design Methodology and Design Applicable Equations
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper presents a systematic methodology, using design applicable equations aided Ka-band Low Noise Amplifier (LNA) design. The LNA design is based on cascode amplifier topology with common-emitter configuration using 0.12$-\mu$m Silicon Germanium (Si-Ge) hetero-junction bipolar transistor (HBT) technology. The designed LNA exhibited a gain S21 greater than 20 dB across the Ka-band frequency range. A noise Figure of less than 3 dB is obtained over the Ka-band. The input reflection coefficient S11 and output reflection coefficient are below -10dB, and the reverse isolation S12 is below −10dB. The systematic methodology is presented as a sectioning of the LNA design into parts that contribute to the performance. Then, by optimizing of the building parts, and the connection between them, we achieve a highly performing LNA. Applicable theory equations are used to optimize performance parameters and synthesize inductors layout. The LNA design provides sufficient gain, low noise Figure and lower circuit complexity. To our knowledge, these are state-of-art results and show validity of the design technique.

articleTitle: GaN Film Grown by Molecular Beam Epitaxy
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: High quality GaN material was obtained on GaN templates under optimized growth conditions. The growth model of GaN was analyzed by Reflection High Energy Electron Diffraction (RHEED). The effect of growth temperature and III/V ratio on the surface of GaN film was studied. The intermediate growth region is the best growth region for GaN, but the growth window is very small. To avoid poor material quality due to entering nitrogen rich growth conditions, the growth is carried out in a slightly metal rich growth region. As the Ga source BEP decreases, the material sequentially transitions from the metal-rich region to the intermediate growth region. The screw dislocations and edge dislocations were estimated from the half-widths of GaN (002) and (102) diffractions. GaN material with smooth surface and low defect concentration of $5\times 10^{8} c \mathrm{m}^{-2}$ was grown under slight Ga-rich regime at 710 °C, which is important for the growth of p-type GaN and the following related other nitride multi-alloys.

articleTitle: A 10-bit 50-MS/s SAR ADC with Binary-Scaled Recombination Weighting Capacitor Array
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: A 10-bit 50MS/s successive-approximation-register (SAR) analog-to-digital converter (ADC) in TSMC 65nm CMOS process with a 1.2-V supply voltage. The DAC capacitor array combines the split monotone control scheme with the monotone control scheme to reduce the offset of the comparator due to the variation of the common-mode input voltage. The DAC structure combined with the binary redundancy recombination method can introduce redundancy to calibrate the errors in the quantization process, reduce the overall quantization time, improve the quantization speed and accuracy. Simulation results show that the SAR ADC achieves 53.36 SNDR and 8.57b ENOB at the input signal of 24.21875 MHz and the sampling rate of 50 MS/s, and consumes 2.72 mW of power.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Ultra-Low Power Consumption for High-Performance SoC
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In order to reduce the power consumption of a System-on-Chip (SoC) with rich peripherals, this paper proposes a systematic ultra-low power optimization design scheme based on multi-voltage design, power gating and clock gating. First, according to the different application scenarios of the SoC and the enabling requirements of the system cores, memories, interface peripherals and other modules, a variety of power consumption modes are formulated. Then the low power consumption intention of the SoC and the Power Management Unit (PMU) are collaboratively designed, and the control method combining software and hardware is used to realize the efficient transition of SoC power consumption mode. This design scheme uses HHG 110nm process to complete logic synthesis and power analysis. Compared with the original design and normal mode, the power consumption of this design in deep sleep mode is reduced by 89.48% and 62.36% respectively, which greatly reduces the power consumption of the SoC. This paper also demonstrates that in nanoscale circuits, this low-power design scheme has a very high power consumption optimization effect.

articleTitle: A Novel SiGe Fin-on-insulator FinFET Device with a SiN Spacer Protection Scheme
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: A novel SiGe fin on insulator (FOI) structure and its FinFET device on a bulk-Si substrate are extensively investigated in this paper. A high-quality SiGe layer epitaxial grown on a Si substrate is realized and a similar notched SiGe/Si fin profile is attained by using the three-step etching process of previous Si FOI structure. However, direct isolation oxidation cannot be applied to get an isolation structure due to lower SiGe thermal stability. Therefore, a SiN film protection post SiGe fin reveal strategy (scheme A) and SiN spacer protection post step-I etching strategy (scheme B) are developed to realize the SiGe FOI structure. Although scheme A can attain a fully oxidation of notched Si fin and no oxidation of SiGe fin, the SiGe fin is distorted due to the large stress induced by the high temperature spike anneal treatment. Compared with the scheme A, a fully isolation of the SiGe fin structure can be achieved and the SiGe fin can maintain well without any oxidation or distorted profile impact. Meanwhile, SiGe FOI FinFET device is also successfully prepared by using the scheme B, which further verifies that it is a practical and effective solution for the fabrication of SiGe FOI structure.

articleTitle: A Low BER Adaptive Sequence Detection Method for High-Speed NRZ Data Transmission
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: To reduce the decision bit error rate (BER) caused by inter symbol interference (ISI) which become more severe as the baud rate of serializer/deserializer (SerDes) interface increases in high-performance computer (HPC) or data center networks, a novel low BER adaptive maximum likelihood sequence estimation (AMLSE) algorithm and its realizable circuit structure for high-speed ADC+DSP SerDes receiver are proposed. In additional, the viterbi algorithm (VA) is adopt to reduce the computational complexity, and the sliding block (SB) technique is proposed to cut the continuous input symbol stream into sliding blocks to achieve parallel decoding and continuous output of symbols in limited resources. An adaptive ISI parameters acquisition algorithm based on an improved zero-forcing (ZF) algorithm is combined to obtain the channel ISI parameters without special training sequence in initialization. The simulation results show that the maximum likelihood sequence estimation (MLSE) method can reduce the BER by up to more than two orders of magnitude and at least by half over DFE for five different fading levels SerDes channels as the baud rates changing from 12G to 56G. While the BER of the AMLSE method is reduced by up to three orders of magnitude and at least by two-thirds relative to ADFE under the same experimental conditions. The adaptive parameters can converge as fast as near 1000 unit interval (UI).

articleTitle: The Stress Analysis of Moisture-Thermal Coupling Based on an Advanced 3D Packaging
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: The three-dimensional (3D) chip stacking package provides numerous advantages to 3D plastic packaging. However, moisture and thermal can pose a risk to the integrity of the package. Hence, it is critical to examine the effects of hygrothermal stress allocation on the reliability of 3D chip stacking packages. Based on the previous work, this paper proposes an innovative 3D chip stacking package structure to study the influence of hygrothermal coupling factors on its reliability. The evolution of packaging structures relies on the continual evolution of the packaging process. This study’s new development structure has not been adequately investigated, particularly in hygrothermal coupling. The constructed 3D stacked package chip is hygrothermal simulated in this work using ANSYS finite element simulation software. Moisture and thermal stresses were coupled. The two were then compared to verify that neither moisture nor thermal stresses are negligible. These packages are subject to the most significant reliability risk impact at the solder ball corners. Thermal moisture stress is more prominent in the lower solder ball than the upper layer and the outer ring than the inner. In this research, the ANSYS tool is used for precise modeling simulation and assessment, providing support and a reference for the smooth simulation of wet thermal coupling in innovative package structures. In addition, the impact of different solder ball sizes on the package is investigated from a practical standpoint. The results provide significant guidance for designing this package’s structure and add to the reliability of the design.

articleTitle: Graph_CC: Accelerator of Connected Component Search in Graph Computing
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: The connected component algorithm is an important basic algorithm for graph computing, which can be applied to scenarios such as network robustness and social network analysis. The connected component algorithm requires high data access and computation overhead to traverse the entire graph to find all connected components, resulting in intensive random memory access and inefficient use of on-chip memory. In order to solve this problem, this paper studies the influence of three different data organization forms on the cache locality of CC algorithm, and selects the storage form of CSCI format with better cache locality. On this basis, this paper designs a connected component search accelerator that can achieve fast addressing: Graph-CC, which stores indexes and data in separate partitions. Through address calculation, sequential addressing can be achieved, and the addressing mode of data in memory is optimized. Using ego-Facebook, p2p-Gnute11a05, and wiki-Vote graph datasets to complete the prototype test of Graph-CC based on the XCVU9P-L2FLGA2104 development board, the results show that compared with accelerators such as ThunderGP, the computing resources are reduced by 22.48%, and the storage resources are reduced by 35.16%, while the throughput is increased by up to 2.75$\times$, and the power consumption efficiency is up to 25.4$\times$.

articleTitle: A High Efficiency Memristor Array Simulation Model for Memristive Neuromorphic Chip Design
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In the design of memristive neuromorphic chip, the memristor array and its peripheral circuits need to be simulated to confirm the correctness of the circuit design. However, almost all existing memristor models are designed for a single device. When array simulation is carried out, a large amount of memristor models need to be instantiated to form an array, which usually consumes huge simulation time and memory. In order to improve the efficiency of circuit simulation, this paper proposes a memristor array simulation model for the design of memristive neuromorphic chips. The model simulates the largesize memristor array by combining the small-size memristor array with the lumped parasitic parameter models, which can accurately simulate the change of the resistance states of the operated devices and the action of the driving circuits, and also reduce the time and memory required for simulation. The experimental results show that, to simulate a 64×64 memristor array, this method can reduce simulation time and memory by 99.21% and 43.15% respectively, than those of instantiating all memristors.

articleTitle: Research and Implementation of Dynamic Reconfigurable Multi-Standard Oriented Coding Block Partition
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: The division of the coding unit is the core module of video coding, which significantly impacts compression efficiency and encoding complexity. The coding block partition circuit implemented by special hardware is difficult to meet the requirements of coding block partition under various standards. The change of the standard needs to redesign the hardware circuit, resulting in a long design cycle and high design cost. A fast partition method of multi-standard coding on dynamic reconfigurable array structure is proposed. This method optimizes the algorithm after analyzing the algorithm, reduces the complexity of the algorithm, and is realized by parallel algorithm mapping. Finally, by changing the controller configuration, the multi-standard algorithm switching can be realized on a single processing element group (PEG). Experimental results show that this method can realize flexible switching of multiple coding multi-standards by hardware, and the clock frequency can reach 126MHz.

articleTitle: Switchable and Tunable Nanolayered Terahertz Metasurfaces Based on the Dual Elliptical-Shaped Array
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Graphene-based terahertz (THz) polarization converters have recently attracted the attention of researchers, but there are few reports on polarization converters with dynamically tunable and switchable properties. Here, a nanolayered metasurface supported with graphene composed of a pair of elliptical-shaped resonators, a bottom gold layer, and a dielectric spacer is proposed as a switchable polarization convertor. Numerical results demonstrated that the proposed design has the advantages of switching between the half-wave plate (HWP) and a quarter-wave plate (QWP) based on graphene in the THz regime. Also, the polarization conversion ratios (PCR) and ellipticity in both working modes are higher than 90% in wide bands. The surface current distributions provide insight into the mechanism of the bi-functional polarization conversions. Thus, the proposed switchable converter shows excellent polarization imaging and communications prospects.

articleTitle: APR-16: The Physical Design of a Reconfigurable Array Processor Chip
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In the physical chip design under the ultra-deep submicron (UDSM) process, interconnect delay, internal resistance drop (IR drop), and signal integrity (SI) has become the key factors affecting timing convergence and design cycle. This paper introduces a reconfigurable array processor architecture chip to solve the above problems. It discusses the requirements of the chip, the logic synthesis, and the physical design under the SMIC 55nm process in detail. First, four different timing optimization methods are employed to optimize the critical path that affects the timing, thus accelerating the execution time of the subsequent placement and routing. Secondly, the edge placement method based on data flow is adopted to reduce the interconnect length and delay of interconnection. Finally, the power network synthesis, placement, clock tree synthesis, and routing are completed. The results demonstrate that the working frequency can reach 320MHz. Meanwhile, the resource consumption is 80506 logic gates, and the chip area is 12mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Dynamic Self-Reconfigurable DCT Transform Unit Supporting Multiple Coding Standards
publicationTitle: 2022 7th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: The implementation of discrete cosine transform (DCT) on dedicated hardware cannot meet the calculation requirements of different residual block sizes in different coding standards. The upgrading of standards requires redesigning DCT unit circuits, resulting in a long design cycle and high design overhead. An implementation method of the DCT transform unit on the dynamic self-reconfigurable array structure driven by a mixed instruction stream and data stream is proposed in this paper. This method is based on the state monitoring mechanism. Monitoring the execution status of the processing element group(PEG) can process in parallel on multiple PEGs and realize the discrete cosine transform supporting various video coding standards on a single platform. The experimental results show that 16 / 8 / 4 pixels can be processed parallel in each clock cycle. The FPGA implementation of the proposed architecture uses a Virtex UltraScale XCVU440 device, running at 126 MHz with a throughput of $2 \times 10\wedge 9$ pixels / s, which can be used as a high-performance hardware accelerator for image and video compression encoding.
